table.name: Torque Reduction Spark Retard
table.description:
Turns a torque or efficiency shortfall back into spark retard on base timing. Besides torque reduction, it is how the ECU pulls fired timing down to Primary Ignition (or the closed-pedal target) plus knock correction advance where that is below Base Timing, so it must stay the inverse of Ignition Efficiency vs Retard; don't edit one without the other. Not used in the rev/overboost-cut states.
Details: When used: on the FFF8A76A spark path (normal fuel mode; the catalyst-heating paths FFF8A76B / FFF8A76C use the sibling Catalyst Heating Spark Retard tables, inferred), except in limit states 0x0B / 0x0C / 0x19 / 0x1A with their Limit-State Spark bits set (stock) and in state 0x1B. 0x0DD568 (read): spark angle FFF8A76A = base timing FFF8A645 - this(max(FFF8A64B, cal 0x2FDE4 = 102) x 128) + per-cylinder trim - tip-in retard FFF8A772, capped at cal 0x1B83C (120); FFF8A76A then rate-limits into the fired timing (0x0DD760 -> 0x0DA600 -> FFF8A744). FFF8A64B (0x0C39DC) is the torque cap over the air torque times the request efficiency, the share of torque the spark must still deliver (inferred), so this is the torque-reduction (and efficiency) retard. Same form as Catalyst Heating Spark Retard (0x0DD4EC). Stock 0 at 100 %, 4 degrees per 1/16 step down to 60 degrees at 12.6 %; the floor 102 limits it to about 34 degrees (inferred). Not used by the rev limiter. The floor applies only on the normal path: when FFF8866C = 3 and either FFF8A649 != -128 or (param 5 = FFF88C64 bit 5 set and the state is not 2), outside state 0x18 with A649 = -128, the input is FFF8AF22 >> 7 instead (no floor, read). FFF8AF22 (0x0C13B4, read) = Ignition Efficiency vs Retard(max(0, FFF8A645 - (FFF8A789 - 32 [+ 0.3516 deg x (KCA FFF8A791 + FLKC FFF8A7A7) in combustion modes 3/4]))), the efficiency of the timing request relative to base timing, and 0x0C39DC builds FFF8A64B = min(255, torque-cap ratio x AF22 / 128). This table is the exact inverse of Ignition Efficiency vs Retard (axis and data mirrored), so on both paths FFF8A76A = min(base timing, timing request + KCA + FLKC) less the torque-cap retard: this is the mechanism by which Primary Ignition (or Closed-Pedal Timing Target) and the knock correction advance limit the fired timing (read; min() form computed). Keep it the inverse of Ignition Efficiency vs Retard. Because FFF8A64B is capped at 255, the pedal-pressed path always takes at least 1 count (0.5 degree) from this table even at full torque (255 x 128 = 32640 -> 1 by the truncating lookup 0x1AB8BC; computed), and the input is always capped at 256 = 100 % (read). LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05BAF8 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00A798. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Base Timing (Pedal Released, TGV Open)
table.description:
Base ignition timing map for the pedal fully released (idle and deceleration) with the TGVs open; from 1200 rpm up its rows equal Base Timing (EGR Off, TGV Open). It is only an upper limit: the ECU fires the lower of this map and Closed-Pedal Timing Target (plus its corrections), and in stock the target is far lower, so raising this map at idle or when coasting does nothing.
Details: When used: Used while the accelerator is fully released (FFF8A774 bit 0, see Base Timing (Pedal Released, TGV Closed)), TGVs not forced closed. table.name: Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 1, Default)
table.description:
Tip-in smoothing for drive mode 1 (the default and fallback mode): how fast the target torque may rise per 10 ms in the first, slow stage of a tip-in, by gear and rpm (scaled by gear and by Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 Pedal Multiplier). Raise for sharper throttle response, lower for smoother. Stock 0.2-0.5 ft-lb (0.25-0.65 Nm) per step.
Details: When used: drive mode other than 2/3/4, FFF88ADA bit 7 set (always in stock) or FFF8AE0A below cal 0x1FC96. Step1, by gear x rpm, before the gear and pedal factors. 0x0BB958 (read; called from the torque module with the limited request FFF8AEC2, the previous output FFF8AEC6, gear FFF8A621, rpm FFF8CD54, drive mode FFF8A8C1 and pedal FFF8AF00): with prev = FFF8AEC6, if prev + Step1 < Stage 2 Torque the shaped value is max(Start Torque, prev + Step1), otherwise max(Stage 2 Torque, prev + Step2); Step1 = (Stage 1 table - 16000) x gear factor (cal 0x1FC98 + 2(g-1): 1, 1, 3, 3, 3 in stock) x Stage 1 Pedal Multiplier(FFF8AF00) / 65025, Step2 the same with cal 0x1FCA2.. (1, 2, 5, 5, 5) and the Stage 2 Pedal Multiplier; the gear factors apply only while FFF8A63D bit 4 is set (else 255 = x1). FFF8AEBE = min(request FFF8AEC2, shaped value). No shaping (FFF8AEBE = request) while the request is below Start Torque, vehicle speed FFF88BE8 is below cal 0x1FCAC (89, about 5 km/h, hysteresis 0x1FCAE), or FFF88ADA bit 6 / FFF88E62 bit 0 is set. So these limit how fast the driver's torque request may rise (tip-in), in two stages. A second shaping path (Path B) exists but is off in stock (Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B). FFF8AEBE goes on through FFF8AEC6 = max(FFF8AEBE, FFF8AEA8) (0x0BD3F0) to the target torque FFF8AECA that indexes boost target and wastegate duty (my research notes). The torque monitor (0x1877B4) reads the same bytes through its own descriptor, so it stays consistent. Drive mode = FFF8A8C1 (2, 3, 4 or other; which value is which SI-Drive position: see the Requested Torque entries, see my research notes). Stock 0.2-0.5 ft-lb (0.25-0.65 Nm) per pass. Same data bytes are also referenced by descriptor(s) 05F6B0. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 0598F8 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 007D28. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 3, Intelligent)
table.description:
Tip-in smoothing for drive mode 3: how fast the target torque may rise per 10 ms in the first, slow stage of a tip-in, by gear and rpm (scaled by gear and by Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 Pedal Multiplier). Raise for sharper throttle response, lower for smoother. Stock 0.2-0.5 ft-lb (0.25-0.65 Nm) per step.
Details: When used: drive mode 3, FFF88ADA bit 7 set (always in stock) or FFF8AE0A below cal 0x1FC96. Step1, by gear x rpm, before the gear and pedal factors. 0x0BB958 (read; called from the torque module with the limited request FFF8AEC2, the previous output FFF8AEC6, gear FFF8A621, rpm FFF8CD54, drive mode FFF8A8C1 and pedal FFF8AF00): with prev = FFF8AEC6, if prev + Step1 < Stage 2 Torque the shaped value is max(Start Torque, prev + Step1), otherwise max(Stage 2 Torque, prev + Step2); Step1 = (Stage 1 table - 16000) x gear factor (cal 0x1FC98 + 2(g-1): 1, 1, 3, 3, 3 in stock) x Stage 1 Pedal Multiplier(FFF8AF00) / 65025, Step2 the same with cal 0x1FCA2.. (1, 2, 5, 5, 5) and the Stage 2 Pedal Multiplier; the gear factors apply only while FFF8A63D bit 4 is set (else 255 = x1). FFF8AEBE = min(request FFF8AEC2, shaped value). No shaping (FFF8AEBE = request) while the request is below Start Torque, vehicle speed FFF88BE8 is below cal 0x1FCAC (89, about 5 km/h, hysteresis 0x1FCAE), or FFF88ADA bit 6 / FFF88E62 bit 0 is set. So these limit how fast the driver's torque request may rise (tip-in), in two stages. A second shaping path (Path B) exists but is off in stock (Target Torque Rise: Enable Path B). FFF8AEBE goes on through FFF8AEC6 = max(FFF8AEBE, FFF8AEA8) (0x0BD3F0) to the target torque FFF8AECA that indexes boost target and wastegate duty (my research notes). The torque monitor (0x1877B4) reads the same bytes through its own descriptor, so it stays consistent. Drive mode = FFF8A8C1 (2, 3, 4 or other; which value is which SI-Drive position: see the Requested Torque entries, see my research notes). Stock 0.2-0.5 ft-lb (0.25-0.65 Nm) per pass. Same data bytes are also referenced by descriptor(s) 05F69C. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 0598E4 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 007D14. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 1, Default, AT/CVT Coding)
table.description:
AT/CVT version of Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 1, Default). Only used on an AT/CVT-coded car, so it has no effect on a manual. Stock 74 ft-lb (100 Nm) per step everywhere, i.e. no Stage 1 limit.
Details: When used: drive mode other than 2/3/4 (1, default) with AT/CVT Coding; unused in stock (manual coding). AT/CVT Coding set = FFF88ADA bit 7 clear and FFF8AE0A >= cal 0x1FC96 (5); FFF88ADA bit 7 is permanently set in stock (my research notes), so the AT/CVT Coding tables are unused on the manual car. Replaces Target Torque Rise Step Stage 1 (Drive Mode 1, Default) (0598F8) as Step1 (read: the selection at 0x0BCB12..0x0BCC20). 0x0BB958 (read; called from the torque module 0x0BE694 at 0x0BF612 with the limited request FFF8AEC2, the previous output FFF8AEC6, gear FFF8A621, rpm FFF8CD54, drive mode FFF8A8C1, pedal FFF8AF00 and, as stack argument 11, cal 0x23704 bit 6; argument order checked in the disassembly). Main path: with prev = FFF8AEC6, if prev + Step1 < Stage 2 Torque the shaped value is max(Start Torque, prev + Step1), otherwise max(Stage 2 Torque, prev + Step2); Step1 = (Stage 1 table - 16000) x gear factor (cal 0x1FC98 + 2(g-1): 1, 1, 3, 3, 3 in stock, 255 = x1) x Stage 1 Pedal Multiplier(FFF8AF00) / 65025, Step2 the same with cal 0x1FCA2.. (1, 2, 5, 5, 5) and the Stage 2 Pedal Multiplier; the gear factors apply only while FFF8A63D bit 4 is set (else x1). FFF8AEBE = min(request FFF8AEC2, shaped value). No shaping (FFF8AEBE = request) while the request is below Start Torque, vehicle speed FFF88BE8 is below cal 0x1FCAC (hysteresis 0x1FCAE), or FFF88ADA bit 6 / FFF88E62 bit 0 is set. FFF8AEBE goes on through FFF8AEC6 = max(FFF8AEBE, FFF8AEA8) (0x0BD3F0) to the target torque FFF8AECA (boost target / wastegate duty axis). Stock 24000 everywhere = 74 ft-lb (100 Nm) per 10 ms, i.e. no Stage 1 limit (same as the high-gear cells of the Stage 2 AT/CVT Coding tables). Its rpm axis (0x2000A) differs from the manual table's. The torque monitor 0x1877B4 reads the same data bytes through its own descriptor (05F674), so it stays consistent. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 0598BC by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 007CEC. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Target Torque Fall Ceiling (Normal)
table.description:
Tip-out smoothing (probably for driveline lash): target torque falls by Step A per 10 ms to the Threshold, then by the smaller Step B. This is the Ceiling, by gear and rpm, for the normal set: the smoothing only acts when the request is below it. Stock 74 ft-lb (100 Nm), 111-148 ft-lb (150-200 Nm) in gears 2-4 above 2000 rpm.

Stock 74 ft-lb (100 Nm), 111-148 ft-lb (150-200 Nm) in gears 2-4 above 2000 rpm. 0x0BB2A4 (read; called with the previous output FFF8AEC6, the rise-shaped request FFF8AEBE, gear FFF8A621, rpm FFF8CD54 and vehicle speed FFF99835): x = FFF8AEC6 - Step A; if x is still >= Threshold, FFF8AEA8 = min(Ceiling, x), else FFF8AEA8 = min(Threshold, FFF8AEC6 - Step B). FFF8AEA8 is used only while FFF8AEBE < Ceiling and FFF88ADA bit 6, FFF88E62 bit 0, FFF8A89F bits 1/2 are clear (else FFF8AEA8 = FFF8AEBE); 0x0BD3F0 sets FFF8AEC6 = max(FFF8AEBE, FFF8AEA8). So when the request drops below Ceiling, the target torque falls by Step A per pass down to Threshold and then by the small Step B: the tip-out ramp (inferred driveline-lash shaping). Table set: vehicle speed < cal 0x20A64 (4 km/h) -> Low Speed set; else FFF8A9A2 bit 7 (latched while FFF8A63E bit 2; not identified) clear -> Normal set, set -> Alternate set. Same data bytes are also referenced by descriptor(s) 05F520. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05977C by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 007BAC. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Rev Limit RPM
table.category: 04.02 Torque & Throttle - Torque Limits & Engine Protection
table.description:
The rev limit (stock 6700 rpm): above it the ECU cuts fuel to all four cylinders on every firing and closes the throttle; spark is not cut or retarded. To move the limit, set this, Rev Limit Full Cut RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM, Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM and Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) to the new rpm and Rev Limit Reset RPM about 100 lower.
Details: When used: always. The rev limit: above this rpm the rev latch sets and the ECU enters limit state 0x0B (part 1); with the stock Full Cut values that is at once a fuel cut on all four cylinders (parts 2-3). It is also the level stage 2 of the throttle cap holds above (part 5). Stock 34304 = 6,700 rpm. Rev limiter and limit-state cuts (LF75404S; read unless marked). The rev limiter is a fuel cut. (1) Limit state, 0x0BE140 (10 ms torque module 0x0BE694): the rev latch FFF8416A sets when rpm FFF8CD54 > Rev Limit RPM (the comparator FFF84169 then uses Rev Limit Reset RPM) and releases once rpm <= Rev Limit Reset RPM and MAP FFF88FF4 < Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP. The overboost latch FFF84167 sets when MAP >= Overboost Limit (compensated, FFF8A851) + Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State) and releases below that level minus Overboost Cut Hysteresis (Limit State). Either latch gives limit state FFF8A639 = 0x0B. Priority: not running = 1, FFF8A640 bit 0 = 0x19, latch FFF8416C = 0x1B (cals 0x22FB2-0x22FBC, not decoded), then 0x0B, then the vehicle-speed latch = 0x0C (see Vehicle Speed Limit). (2) Full-cut latch, 0x0BAE98: FFF840C4 sets when rpm >= Rev Limit Full Cut RPM and releases once rpm <= Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM and MAP < Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP (above Rev Limit Full Cut Speed Threshold the pair Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM / Stage 2 RPM is used instead; never in stock). In state 0x0B the final torque cap FFF8AE54 (0x0B9DC8) is limited to FFF8AE8A: zero indicated torque (32000 - losses FFF8AF62) while this latch or the overboost flag FFF8A63A bit 6 (Overboost Limit + Overboost Margin for Overboost Delay) is set, otherwise FFF8AF3A = the current air torque minus losses, i.e. no reduction. (3) Fuel: 0x0C4BA0 turns the cap into the torque ratio FFF8A64F; in limit states 8, 9, 0x0B, 0x0C and 0x18-0x1B, 0x0C1AC8 turns the ratio into the number of cylinders to cut FFF8A643 (Cylinder Cut Torque Ratio thresholds; a zero cap gives 4). Once per combustion event (crank-synchronous list 0x07D0E0) 0x0C4B84 makes a cut decision FFF8A648 from the count and the last three decisions (4 = every event, 3 = three in four, 2 = every second, 1 = one in four; the pattern is in code, not a cal). 0x0C88C8 (list 0x07D1C2) latches it into the cut flag of the cylinder being scheduled (FFF8A6F5-FFF8A6F8). For a flagged cylinder the fuel time is 0 (0x0D1D7C/0x0D1FB8) and both start angles are 0x1FE (0x0CB394/0x0CB604), which the injector driver 0x1DCA04 treats as no pulse. So the cut is a true injector cut, all four cylinders, every event. (4) Spark is neither cut nor retarded: the coil scheduler 0x1DB804 only checks FFF8C6F4 (set at the first injection after sync, cleared only on stop), and with Limit-State Spark: Normal Target in Rev/Overboost Cut set (stock) 0x0DD568 uses the normal spark target FFF8A72A in state 0x0B instead of Torque Reduction Spark Retard. (5) Throttle: with Rev/Boost Limit Torque Caps Enable set (stock) 0x0BDA84 caps the throttle-side request FFF8AE4C in state 0x0B by 0x0BAFA8: Rev/Boost Limit Torque (Stage 1) while rpm > Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM (held while > Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold)) or MAP FFF8AF70 > Rev/Boost Limit Torque Stage 1 MAP (held while > Stage 1 Reset MAP); else (Stage 2) while rpm > Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) (held while > Rev Limit RPM) or MAP > Stage 1 Reset MAP (held while > Stage 2 Hold MAP); else (Base). The torque monitor (0x186F0C) repeats this with the same data. Stock behaviour: above 6,700 rpm all four injectors are cut every event, the throttle closes toward a 37 ft-lb (50 Nm) request and the spark is unchanged; fuel returns as soon as rpm is back at 6,700 or below with MAP under 168 kPa abs (no rpm hysteresis on the fuel cut), and the Base throttle cap (about 166 ft-lb, 225 Nm there, rarely binding) lasts until 6,600 rpm. A hard cut; stage 2 is never selected because its thresholds equal stage 1's. To move the limit, set Rev Limit RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM, Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM and Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) to the new rpm and Rev Limit Reset RPM about 100 rpm lower. Setting the Full Cut pair above Rev Limit RPM gives a throttle-only soft stage between them (inferred). The Fail-Safe Rev Limit cals (6,100 rpm) cut fuel the same way, in any state, when their fault flags are set. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 01DEDE by the code that reads it (read). Address 02440E. Confidence: read.

table.name: Rev Limit Full Cut RPM
table.category: 04.02 Torque & Throttle - Torque Limits & Engine Protection
table.description:
At or above this rpm, once the rev limit has started, every injector is cut on every firing (a hard fuel cut). Keep it equal to Rev Limit RPM; set higher, the range between them gets only the throttle cap, probably a softer limit. Stock 6700 rpm.
Details: When used: always in stock (vehicle speed never exceeds Rev Limit Full Cut Speed Threshold). Set rpm of the full-cut latch (part 2): at or above it, while state 0x0B is active, the torque cap is zero and all four injectors are cut every combustion event (part 3). On its own it does not start a cut; Rev Limit RPM does. Set above Rev Limit RPM, the range between them gets only the throttle cap (part 5; a soft stage, inferred). Stock 34304 = 6,700 rpm. Rev limiter and limit-state cuts (LF75404S; read unless marked). The rev limiter is a fuel cut. Either latch gives limit state FFF8A639 = 0x0B. table.name: Maximum Torque (IAT)
table.category: 04.02 Torque & Throttle - Torque Limits & Engine Protection
table.description:
Maximum target torque by rpm and intake air temperature. The ECU uses the lowest of this, Maximum Torque (DAM) and other limits, and the result drives the boost target. Stock 258 ft-lb (350 Nm) warm from about 2000 rpm; less at low rpm, with very cold intake air below about 3000 rpm, and above about 6000 rpm with intake air at or below 32 F (148-170 ft-lb, 200-230 Nm, back to full by 50 F).

table.name: Overboost Limit
table.category: 04.02 Torque & Throttle - Torque Limits & Engine Protection
table.description:

Details: When used: always. 0x1087D4 (20 ms boost task) -> FFF8A850 (raw) and FFF8A851 = (raw + 13.3) x f - 13, f = the boost target's baro/IAT factor FFF8B3B2/32768 (read; cal 0x290A8 = 1 would use a fixed value, 0 in stock). Two overboost reactions use FFF8A851 (read): (a) 0x0C0FE0 (10 ms): MAP FFF88FF4 >= this + Overboost Margin for Overboost Delay passes in a row sets the overboost flag FFF8A63A bit 6, cleared when MAP <= this + Overboost Flag Reset Margin; (b) 0x0BE140: MAP >= this + Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State) puts the ECU in limit state 0x0B, which caps the throttle at once. Confidence: read.

table.name: Rev/Boost Limit Torque (Base)
table.category: 04.02 Torque & Throttle - Torque Limits & Engine Protection
table.description:
Throttle-side torque cap by rpm used only during the rev or overboost cut when neither stage applies. It does not limit torque in normal driving, so raising it gives no extra power. Stock about 165 ft-lb (224 Nm) near the limiter, 108-207 ft-lb (146-280 Nm) lower down.
Details: When used: only in limit state 0x0B while neither stage cap is on: in stock after a rev cut between Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM and Rev Limit Reset RPM, and during an overboost cut below 256 kPa abs. Throttle-side torque cap by rpm FFF8CD54 (part 5); it is not a general torque limit: outside state 0x0B the request passes uncapped (0x0BDA84, read), so raising it gives no extra torque in normal driving (the normal-driving caps are Maximum Torque (IAT) / (DAM)). It limits the throttle only, not fuel or spark. Stock 108 ft-lb (146 Nm) at 1,200 rpm, 207 ft-lb (280 Nm) at 2,000 rpm, about 192 ft-lb (260 Nm) at 2,800-3,600 rpm, 184 ft-lb (250 Nm) at 4,400-6,000 rpm and 165 ft-lb (224 Nm) from 6,800 rpm. Rev limiter and limit-state cuts (LF75404S; read unless marked). The rev limiter is a fuel cut. (1) Limit state, 0x0BE140 (10 ms torque module 0x0BE694): the rev latch FFF8416A sets when rpm FFF8CD54 > Rev Limit RPM (the comparator FFF84169 then uses Rev Limit Reset RPM) and releases once rpm <= Rev Limit Reset RPM and MAP FFF88FF4 < Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP. The overboost latch FFF84167 sets when MAP >= Overboost Limit (compensated, FFF8A851) + Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State) and releases below that level minus Overboost Cut Hysteresis (Limit State). Either latch gives limit state FFF8A639 = 0x0B. Priority: not running = 1, FFF8A640 bit 0 = 0x19, latch FFF8416C = 0x1B (cals 0x22FB2-0x22FBC, not decoded), then 0x0B, then the vehicle-speed latch = 0x0C (see Vehicle Speed Limit). (2) Full-cut latch, 0x0BAE98: FFF840C4 sets when rpm >= Rev Limit Full Cut RPM and releases once rpm <= Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM and MAP < Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP (above Rev Limit Full Cut Speed Threshold the pair Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM / Stage 2 RPM is used instead; never in stock). In state 0x0B the final torque cap FFF8AE54 (0x0B9DC8) is limited to FFF8AE8A: zero indicated torque (32000 - losses FFF8AF62) while this latch or the overboost flag FFF8A63A bit 6 (Overboost Limit + Overboost Margin for Overboost Delay) is set, otherwise FFF8AF3A = the current air torque minus losses, i.e. no reduction. (3) Fuel: 0x0C4BA0 turns the cap into the torque ratio FFF8A64F; in limit states 8, 9, 0x0B, 0x0C and 0x18-0x1B, 0x0C1AC8 turns the ratio into the number of cylinders to cut FFF8A643 (Cylinder Cut Torque Ratio thresholds; a zero cap gives 4). Once per combustion event (crank-synchronous list 0x07D0E0) 0x0C4B84 makes a cut decision FFF8A648 from the count and the last three decisions (4 = every event, 3 = three in four, 2 = every second, 1 = one in four; the pattern is in code, not a cal). 0x0C88C8 (list 0x07D1C2) latches it into the cut flag of the cylinder being scheduled (FFF8A6F5-FFF8A6F8). For a flagged cylinder the fuel time is 0 (0x0D1D7C/0x0D1FB8) and both start angles are 0x1FE (0x0CB394/0x0CB604), which the injector driver 0x1DCA04 treats as no pulse. So the cut is a true injector cut, all four cylinders, every event. (4) Spark is neither cut nor retarded: the coil scheduler 0x1DB804 only checks FFF8C6F4 (set at the first injection after sync, cleared only on stop), and with Limit-State Spark: Normal Target in Rev/Overboost Cut set (stock) 0x0DD568 uses the normal spark target FFF8A72A in state 0x0B instead of Torque Reduction Spark Retard. (5) Throttle: with Rev/Boost Limit Torque Caps Enable set (stock) 0x0BDA84 caps the throttle-side request FFF8AE4C in state 0x0B by 0x0BAFA8: Rev/Boost Limit Torque (Stage 1) while rpm > Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM (held while > Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold)) or MAP FFF8AF70 > Rev/Boost Limit Torque Stage 1 MAP (held while > Stage 1 Reset MAP); else (Stage 2) while rpm > Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) (held while > Rev Limit RPM) or MAP > Stage 1 Reset MAP (held while > Stage 2 Hold MAP); else (Base). The torque monitor (0x186F0C) repeats this with the same data. Stock behaviour: above 6,700 rpm all four injectors are cut every event, the throttle closes toward a 37 ft-lb (50 Nm) request and the spark is unchanged; fuel returns as soon as rpm is back at 6,700 or below with MAP under 168 kPa abs (no rpm hysteresis on the fuel cut), and the Base throttle cap (about 166 ft-lb, 225 Nm there, rarely binding) lasts until 6,600 rpm. A hard cut; stage 2 is never selected because its thresholds equal stage 1's. To move the limit, set Rev Limit RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM, Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM and Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) to the new rpm and Rev Limit Reset RPM about 100 rpm lower. Setting the Full Cut pair above Rev Limit RPM gives a throttle-only soft stage between them (inferred). The Fail-Safe Rev Limit cals (6,100 rpm) cut fuel the same way, in any state, when their fault flags are set. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 0596BC by the code that reads it (read). (2) Full-cut latch, 0x0BAE98: FFF840C4 sets when rpm >= Rev Limit Full Cut RPM and releases once rpm <= Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM and MAP < Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP (above Rev Limit Full Cut Speed Threshold the pair Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM / Stage 2 RPM is used instead; never in stock). In state 0x0B the final torque cap FFF8AE54 (0x0B9DC8) is limited to FFF8AE8A: zero indicated torque (32000 - losses FFF8AF62) while this latch or the overboost flag FFF8A63A bit 6 (Overboost Limit + Overboost Margin for Overboost Delay) is set, otherwise FFF8AF3A = the current air torque minus losses, i.e. no reduction. (3) Fuel: 0x0C4BA0 turns the cap into the torque ratio FFF8A64F; in limit states 8, 9, 0x0B, 0x0C and 0x18-0x1B, 0x0C1AC8 turns the ratio into the number of cylinders to cut FFF8A643 (Cylinder Cut Torque Ratio thresholds; a zero cap gives 4). Once per combustion event (crank-synchronous list 0x07D0E0) 0x0C4B84 makes a cut decision FFF8A648 from the count and the last three decisions (4 = every event, 3 = three in four, 2 = every second, 1 = one in four; the pattern is in code, not a cal). 0x0C88C8 (list 0x07D1C2) latches it into the cut flag of the cylinder being scheduled (FFF8A6F5-FFF8A6F8). For a flagged cylinder the fuel time is 0 (0x0D1D7C/0x0D1FB8) and both start angles are 0x1FE (0x0CB394/0x0CB604), which the injector driver 0x1DCA04 treats as no pulse. So the cut is a true injector cut, all four cylinders, every event. (4) Spark is neither cut nor retarded: the coil scheduler 0x1DB804 only checks FFF8C6F4 (set at the first injection after sync, cleared only on stop), and with Limit-State Spark: Normal Target in Rev/Overboost Cut set (stock) 0x0DD568 uses the normal spark target FFF8A72A in state 0x0B instead of Torque Reduction Spark Retard. (5) Throttle: with Rev/Boost Limit Torque Caps Enable set (stock) 0x0BDA84 caps the throttle-side request FFF8AE4C in state 0x0B by 0x0BAFA8: Rev/Boost Limit Torque (Stage 1) while rpm > Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM (held while > Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold)) or MAP FFF8AF70 > Rev/Boost Limit Torque Stage 1 MAP (held while > Stage 1 Reset MAP); else (Stage 2) while rpm > Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) (held while > Rev Limit RPM) or MAP > Stage 1 Reset MAP (held while > Stage 2 Hold MAP); else (Base). The torque monitor (0x186F0C) repeats this with the same data. Stock behaviour: above 6,700 rpm all four injectors are cut every event, the throttle closes toward a 37 ft-lb (50 Nm) request and the spark is unchanged; fuel returns as soon as rpm is back at 6,700 or below with MAP under 168 kPa abs (no rpm hysteresis on the fuel cut), and the Base throttle cap (about 166 ft-lb, 225 Nm there, rarely binding) lasts until 6,600 rpm. A hard cut; stage 2 is never selected because its thresholds equal stage 1's. To move the limit, set Rev Limit RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM, Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM and Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) to the new rpm and Rev Limit Reset RPM about 100 rpm lower. Setting the Full Cut pair above Rev Limit RPM gives a throttle-only soft stage between them (inferred). The Fail-Safe Rev Limit cals (6,100 rpm) cut fuel the same way, in any state, when their fault flags are set. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 01DE86 by the code that reads it (read). Address 0243B6. Confidence: read.

table.name: Rev/Boost Limit Torque Caps Enable [byte, bit 0 = 1]
table.category: 04.02 Torque & Throttle - Torque Limits & Engine Protection
table.description:
Bit 0 of this byte (value 1) is the switch: add 1 to set it, subtract 1 to clear it; leave the other bits as they are. Lets the rev limiter and overboost cut close the throttle (the Rev/Boost Limit Torque tables). Set in stock; cleared, the limiter is probably fuel-cut only.
Details: Set in stock. With this bit set, 0x0BDA84 replaces the throttle-side request FFF8AE4C by the Rev/Boost Limit Torque cap FFF8AE8C (0x0BAFA8) in limit state 0x0B; the torque monitor 0x189488 reads the same bit (read). Cleared, the rev limiter and the overboost cut become fuel-only: no throttle closing during the cut (inferred). LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 023CEA by the code that reads it (read). Address 02AF9E bit 0 (value 1). Confidence: read.

table.name: Overboost Margin
table.category: 04.02 Torque & Throttle - Torque Limits & Engine Protection
table.description:
How far above Overboost Limit boost must be before overboost time is counted toward the overboost flag, which makes the overboost cut a full fuel cut. Stock 26.7 kPa (3.9 psi).
Details: When used: always. 0x0C0FE0: overboost time is counted while MAP FFF88FF4 >= Overboost Limit + this (read); after Overboost Delay the flag FFF8A63A bit 6 sets. The flag makes the limit-state overboost cut (Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State)) a full fuel cut on all four cylinders; it has no effect outside that state (read). Stock 6835 = 26.7 kPa (3.9 psi). LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 01DEF4 by the code that reads it (read). Address 024424. Confidence: read.

table.name: Overboost Delay
table.category: 04.02 Torque & Throttle - Torque Limits & Engine Protection
table.description:
How long boost must stay above Overboost Limit plus Overboost Margin before the overboost flag sets and the overboost cut becomes a full fuel cut. Stock 2.0 s.
Details: When used: always. 0x0C0FE0: consecutive 10 ms passes with MAP >= Overboost Limit + Overboost Margin before the overboost flag FFF8A63A bit 6 sets (read); the count restarts when MAP drops below that level. The flag turns the limit-state overboost cut into a full fuel cut on all four cylinders (see Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State)). Stock 200 = 2.0 s. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 01DEF8 by the code that reads it (read). Address 024428. Confidence: read.

table.name: Overboost Flag Reset Margin
table.category: 04.02 Torque & Throttle - Torque Limits & Engine Protection
table.description:
Once set, the overboost flag clears only when boost falls to Overboost Limit plus this. Stock 0 kPa.
Details: When used: always. 0x0C0FE0 (read): once set, the overboost flag FFF8A63A bit 6 (Overboost Limit + Overboost Margin for Overboost Delay) stays set until MAP FFF88FF4 <= Overboost Limit + this. The flag forces the zero torque cap in the overboost/rev cut state (0x0BAE98 -> FFF8AE8A, applied in limit state 0x0B; Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State)) and also feeds 0x1B8310 (0x1B828C / 0x1B83CC, the overboost diagnostic, inferred in my research notes), so this margin also sets how long that monitor sees overboost. Stock 0. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 01DEF6 by the calibration block offset of its neighbours (inferred). Address 024426. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State)
table.category: 04.02 Torque & Throttle - Torque Limits & Engine Protection
table.description:
Boost above Overboost Limit plus this enters the overboost cut state: the throttle is capped at once, and fuel to all cylinders is cut only if the 2-second overboost flag is also set. Stock 33 kPa.
Details: When used: always. Overboost latch FFF84167 (0x0BE140, read): sets when MAP FFF88FF4 >= Overboost Limit (the baro/IAT-compensated FFF8A851) + this, and releases when MAP < that level minus Overboost Cut Hysteresis (Limit State). While set (and no higher state) the limit state FFF8A639 is 0x0B, the same state as the rev limiter (see Rev Limit RPM). In that state the throttle-side request is capped at once (Rev/Boost Limit Torque (Base) by rpm, or the stage tables above 256 kPa abs); fuel is cut on all four cylinders every event only once the overboost flag FFF8A63A bit 6 is also set (MAP >= Overboost Limit + Overboost Margin for Overboost Delay, 2.0 s stock) or rpm reaches Rev Limit Full Cut RPM; spark is not retarded. When MAP falls below the release level the state ends and fuel returns even if the flag is still set (inferred from the state gating, read). Stock 8448 = 33 kPa, about 244 kPa abs at the 211 kPa stock limit peak. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 01DEE6 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: (read) Counterpart reader(s) 0x0BE140->0x0C6814 (ref 1 access(es), target 1, size [2]); decompile token alignment puts this cal at the position of LF75404S 0x01DEE6 (1 reference(s), votes {'024416': 1}); machine-code effective addresses of the target function confirm 0x024416 is accessed as u16. Stock 8448 (LF75404S 8448). Matches the layout address. Address 024416. Confidence: read.

table.name: Overboost Cut Hysteresis (Limit State)
table.category: 04.02 Torque & Throttle - Torque Limits & Engine Protection
table.description:
How far boost must fall below the overboost cut level before the overboost cut state ends. Stock 15 kPa.
Details: When used: always. Subtracted from the overboost latch level while the latch FFF84167 is set (0x0BE208-0x0BE222, read): the overboost cut state 0x0B releases when MAP FFF88FF4 < Overboost Limit + Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State) - this. See Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State) for what the state does. Stock 3840 = 15 kPa, so the state releases 18 kPa above the Overboost Limit. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 01DEE8 by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: (read) Counterpart reader(s) 0x0BE140->0x0C6814 (ref 2 access(es), target 2, size [2]); decompile token alignment puts this cal at the position of LF75404S 0x01DEE8 (2 reference(s), votes {'024418': 2}); machine-code effective addresses of the target function confirm 0x024418 is accessed as u16. Stock 3840 (LF75404S 3840). Matches the layout address. Address 024418. Confidence: read.

table.name: Vehicle Speed Limit
table.category: 04.02 Torque & Throttle - Torque Limits & Engine Protection
table.description:
Vehicle speed limiter. It needs this speed, Vehicle Speed Limit Minimum RPM and Vehicle Speed Limit Full Cut Speed to act, and then cuts fuel to all cylinders without closing the throttle. Stock 255 km/h with a 6375 rpm minimum: off (no effect in stock).
Details: When used: always (off in stock). Set speed of the vehicle-speed latch FFF84168 (0x0BE140, read): it sets when vehicle speed FFF99835 >= this minus Vehicle Speed Limit Offset and engine speed FFF8CD5C (rpm/25) >= Vehicle Speed Limit Minimum RPM, and holds until speed is below that level and MAP FFF88FF4 <= Vehicle Speed Limit Reset Maximum MAP. While it is set (and no higher state), the limit state FFF8A639 is 0x0C. State 0x0C does not reduce torque by itself: the final torque cap FFF8AE54 is limited (0x0B9DC8) to FFF8AF1A (0x0C058C), which is zero torque only while speed >= Vehicle Speed Limit Full Cut Speed (then all four injectors are cut every event through the cylinder-cut count FFF8A643, see Rev Limit RPM part 3), otherwise the current torque. There is no throttle cap in state 0x0C (0x0BDA84 caps only state 0x0B) and the spark stays on its normal target (Limit-State Spark: Normal Target in Speed Limit). Fuel trims for state 0x0C (cals 0x3845C-0x3845F, by number of cylinders cut) are 0 in stock (0x0C558C, Ghidra stack arguments, not checked). Stock 255 km/h with a 6,375 rpm minimum and a 255 km/h full-cut speed: off. A working speed limiter needs this, Vehicle Speed Limit Full Cut Speed and Vehicle Speed Limit Minimum RPM (inferred); it is then a hard fuel cut. Limit-state priority: not running 1, FFF8A640 bit 0 0x19, latch FFF8416C 0x1B, rev/overboost 0x0B, speed 0x0C (0x0BE37E-0x0BE476, read). LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 01DEDC by the code that reads it (read). Address 02440C. Confidence: read.

table.name: Vehicle Speed Limit Minimum RPM
table.category: 04.02 Torque & Throttle - Torque Limits & Engine Protection
table.description:
The speed limiter only starts at or above this engine speed. Stock 6375 rpm, part of why the speed limiter is off in stock.
Details: When used: always (off in stock). The vehicle-speed latch (state 0x0C, see Vehicle Speed Limit) sets only while engine speed FFF8CD5C (rpm/25) >= this (0x0BE1E8-0x0BE1F4, read). Stock 255 = 6,375 rpm, which together with the 255 km/h limit keeps the speed limiter off. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 01DEEC by the code that reads it (read). Address 02441C. Confidence: read.

table.name: Vehicle Speed Limit Full Cut Speed
table.category: 04.02 Torque & Throttle - Torque Limits & Engine Protection
table.description:
Speed at which the active speed limiter cuts fuel to all cylinders; without it the limiter does nothing. Stock 255 km/h (no effect in stock).
Details: When used: only in limit state 0x0C (vehicle-speed latch, see Vehicle Speed Limit). 0x0C058C (read): latch FFF84188 sets when vehicle speed FFF99835 >= this (minus Vehicle Speed Limit Full Cut Speed Hysteresis while above it) and holds until speed is below and MAP <= Vehicle Speed Limit Reset Maximum MAP; while set, FFF8AF1A = zero torque, which in state 0x0C cuts fuel on all four cylinders every event (0x0B9DC8, 0x0C1AC8). Without it state 0x0C reduces nothing. Stock 255 km/h (off). LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 01DEF9 by the calibration block offset of its neighbours (inferred). Address 024429. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Vehicle Speed Limit Full Cut Speed Hysteresis
table.category: 04.02 Torque & Throttle - Torque Limits & Engine Protection
table.description:
How far speed must fall below Vehicle Speed Limit Full Cut Speed before the fuel cut ends. Stock 2 km/h; no effect in stock.
Details: When used: only in limit state 0x0C. Subtracted from Vehicle Speed Limit Full Cut Speed after a pass at or above it (FFF8418A), so the full cut holds down to that speed (0x0C058C, read). Stock 2 km/h. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 023700 by the code that reads it (read). Address 02A9B4. Confidence: read.

table.name: Vehicle Speed Limit Offset
table.category: 04.02 Torque & Throttle - Torque Limits & Engine Protection
table.description:
Subtracted from Vehicle Speed Limit to give the speed where the limiter state starts; it is not a release hysteresis. Stock 2 km/h; no effect in stock.
Details: When used: always (the speed limiter is off in stock). Subtracted from Vehicle Speed Limit in the set test of the speed latch FFF84168 (0x0BE1CA-0x0BE1E4, read), so the latch sets at Vehicle Speed Limit minus this. It is not a release hysteresis: the latch releases when speed is below the same level and MAP <= Vehicle Speed Limit Reset Maximum MAP (read). See Vehicle Speed Limit for what the latch does (state 0x0C). Stock 2 km/h. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 01DEE2 by the code that reads it (read). Address 024412. Confidence: read.

table.name: Vehicle Speed Limit Reset Maximum MAP
table.category: 04.02 Torque & Throttle - Torque Limits & Engine Protection
table.description:
The speed limiter cannot release while manifold pressure is above this. Stock 168 kPa absolute; no effect in stock.
Details: When used: always (off in stock). Neither the vehicle-speed latch FFF84168 (0x0BE140) nor the speed full-cut latch FFF84188 (0x0C058C) releases while MAP FFF88FF4 is above this, even below its speed (read). Confidence: read.

table.name: Vehicle Speed Limit Reset Maximum MAP Hysteresis
table.category: 04.02 Torque & Throttle - Torque Limits & Engine Protection
table.description:
Hysteresis on Vehicle Speed Limit Reset Maximum MAP. Stock 0; no effect in stock.
Details: When used: always (off in stock). Added to Vehicle Speed Limit Reset Maximum MAP after a pass with MAP at or below it (FFF84165 / FFF84189), saturating (0x0BE270-0x0BE28E, 0x0C058C, read). Stock 0. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 01DEF0 by the code that reads it (read). Address 024420. Confidence: read.

table.name: Rev Limit Full Cut Speed Threshold Hysteresis
table.category: 04.02 Torque & Throttle - Torque Limits & Engine Protection

Details: When used: always, no effect in stock. Stock 0. Rev limiter and limit-state cuts (LF75404S; read unless marked). The rev limiter is a fuel cut. (1) Limit state, 0x0BE140 (10 ms torque module 0x0BE694): the rev latch FFF8416A sets when rpm FFF8CD54 > Rev Limit RPM (the comparator FFF84169 then uses Rev Limit Reset RPM) and releases once rpm <= Rev Limit Reset RPM and MAP FFF88FF4 < Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP. The overboost latch FFF84167 sets when MAP >= Overboost Limit (compensated, FFF8A851) + Overboost Cut Margin (Limit State) and releases below that level minus Overboost Cut Hysteresis (Limit State). Either latch gives limit state FFF8A639 = 0x0B. Priority: not running = 1, FFF8A640 bit 0 = 0x19, latch FFF8416C = 0x1B (cals 0x22FB2-0x22FBC, not decoded), then 0x0B, then the vehicle-speed latch = 0x0C (see Vehicle Speed Limit). (2) Full-cut latch, 0x0BAE98: FFF840C4 sets when rpm >= Rev Limit Full Cut RPM and releases once rpm <= Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM and MAP < Rev Limit Reset Maximum MAP (above Rev Limit Full Cut Speed Threshold the pair Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM / Stage 2 RPM is used instead; never in stock). In state 0x0B the final torque cap FFF8AE54 (0x0B9DC8) is limited to FFF8AE8A: zero indicated torque (32000 - losses FFF8AF62) while this latch or the overboost flag FFF8A63A bit 6 (Overboost Limit + Overboost Margin for Overboost Delay) is set, otherwise FFF8AF3A = the current air torque minus losses, i.e. no reduction. (3) Fuel: 0x0C4BA0 turns the cap into the torque ratio FFF8A64F; in limit states 8, 9, 0x0B, 0x0C and 0x18-0x1B, 0x0C1AC8 turns the ratio into the number of cylinders to cut FFF8A643 (Cylinder Cut Torque Ratio thresholds; a zero cap gives 4). Once per combustion event (crank-synchronous list 0x07D0E0) 0x0C4B84 makes a cut decision FFF8A648 from the count and the last three decisions (4 = every event, 3 = three in four, 2 = every second, 1 = one in four; the pattern is in code, not a cal). 0x0C88C8 (list 0x07D1C2) latches it into the cut flag of the cylinder being scheduled (FFF8A6F5-FFF8A6F8). For a flagged cylinder the fuel time is 0 (0x0D1D7C/0x0D1FB8) and both start angles are 0x1FE (0x0CB394/0x0CB604), which the injector driver 0x1DCA04 treats as no pulse. So the cut is a true injector cut, all four cylinders, every event. (4) Spark is neither cut nor retarded: the coil scheduler 0x1DB804 only checks FFF8C6F4 (set at the first injection after sync, cleared only on stop), and with Limit-State Spark: Normal Target in Rev/Overboost Cut set (stock) 0x0DD568 uses the normal spark target FFF8A72A in state 0x0B instead of Torque Reduction Spark Retard. (5) Throttle: with Rev/Boost Limit Torque Caps Enable set (stock) 0x0BDA84 caps the throttle-side request FFF8AE4C in state 0x0B by 0x0BAFA8: Rev/Boost Limit Torque (Stage 1) while rpm > Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM (held while > Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold)) or MAP FFF8AF70 > Rev/Boost Limit Torque Stage 1 MAP (held while > Stage 1 Reset MAP); else (Stage 2) while rpm > Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) (held while > Rev Limit RPM) or MAP > Stage 1 Reset MAP (held while > Stage 2 Hold MAP); else (Base). The torque monitor (0x186F0C) repeats this with the same data. Stock behaviour: above 6,700 rpm all four injectors are cut every event, the throttle closes toward a 37 ft-lb (50 Nm) request and the spark is unchanged; fuel returns as soon as rpm is back at 6,700 or below with MAP under 168 kPa abs (no rpm hysteresis on the fuel cut), and the Base throttle cap (about 166 ft-lb, 225 Nm there, rarely binding) lasts until 6,600 rpm. A hard cut; stage 2 is never selected because its thresholds equal stage 1's. To move the limit, set Rev Limit RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut RPM, Rev Limit Full Cut Reset RPM, Rev Limit Stage 1 RPM and Rev Limit Stage 2 RPM (Stage 1 Hold) to the new rpm and Rev Limit Reset RPM about 100 rpm lower. Setting the Full Cut pair above Rev Limit RPM gives a throttle-only soft stage between them (inferred). The Fail-Safe Rev Limit cals (6,100 rpm) cut fuel the same way, in any state, when their fault flags are set. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 01DEEB by its caller in the decompiled code (read). Evidence: the counterpart of LF75404S 0x0BAE98, overrev function (seg_0x0C0000.c:2727): speed threshold 02441A (+ hysteresis 02441B), and while at or below it the set/reset rpm 02435C / 02435A (read); same structure as the reference. Address 02441B. Confidence: read.

table.name: Fail-Safe Rev Limit (Rail Pressure Fault)
table.category: 04.02 Torque & Throttle - Torque Limits & Engine Protection
table.description:

Details: When used: only while fault flag FFF88EDA bit 5 or 7 (set by 0x080B96 from rail-pressure monitor bits FFF89BDE 0-3, next to the P0087/P0088 bits, inferred) or FFF88E2C bit 2 (pending P0192/P0193, rail pressure sensor) is set. 0x0C1AC8 (read): limit FFF8AF4C = the lowest of this and the other active Fail-Safe Rev Limit cals (65535 when none), and FFF8AF4A = max(FFF8AF4C, idle target FFF8B236 + Fail-Safe Rev Limit Minimum Above Idle Target). While rpm >= FFF8AF4A (release Fail-Safe Rev Limit Hysteresis lower) the cylinder-cut count FFF8A643 is forced to 4: all four injectors are cut every event, in any limit state (same injector path as Rev Limit RPM part 3). table.description:

table.description:

table.name: Throttle Opening (Required Area)
table.category: 04.03 Torque & Throttle - Throttle Control & Throttle Model

table.name: Required Throttle Area FFF8AFB4 (mm^2 (effective throttle area))

table.description:
Converts the required throttle area into commanded throttle opening (%). It is the exact inverse of Throttle Area from Opening; keep the two consistent, and edit Throttle Opening (Monitor) too. Leave alone unless the throttle body changes. Area is in mm^2 of effective throttle opening (about 2,150 mm^2 wide open).
Details: 0x0C326C (read): commanded throttle FFF8AF84 = this(max(Throttle Required Area output FFF8AFB4, idle area FFF8AE00)) x 400 / cal 0x3826E (706); 25600 = 100 % (OBD PID 0x4C, SSM 0x15, logger J11). The accelerator pedal FFF88824 x 100/256 is added only with the engine stopped (state 1) or with cal 0x23D0C bit 0 set (clear in stock), never while running. Stock 0 % at area 18 to 99.9 % at 21468 (wide open). It is the exact inverse of Throttle Area from Opening; keep the two consistent. The same data is also read as 05A170 (idle floor) and 060B10. The monitor copy Throttle Opening (Monitor) (05F3FC, data 0x048EE6) must be edited too. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05A0BC by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 008608. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Throttle Opening (Monitor)
table.category: 04.03 Torque & Throttle - Throttle Control & Throttle Model
table.description:
Throttle-monitor copy of Throttle Opening (Required Area). Identical in stock; edit both together. Area is in mm^2 of effective throttle opening (about 2,150 mm^2 wide open).
Details: 0x185DD8 (read): separate copy (data 0x048EE6, axis 0x048F06) of Throttle Opening 05A0BC with its own divisor cal 0x48F5A (706); identical in stock. Edit together with 05A0BC. Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05F3FC by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00E584. Confidence: read.

table.name: Throttle Required Area
table.category: 04.03 Torque & Throttle - Throttle Control & Throttle Model
table.description:
Throttle area needed for a given fraction of full-load torque, by rpm. At part throttle it cancels out against Torque Fraction from Throttle Area, so part-throttle feel is set by the Throttle Opening from Target Torque maps instead. If you edit it, edit it with Torque Fraction from Throttle Area and Throttle Required Area (Monitor). Area is in mm^2 of effective throttle opening (about 2,150 mm^2 wide open).
Details: Columns: FFF8AFA8 = (torque request + losses) / (full-load reference torque) x spark compensation (0x0C37D8, read), i.e. the requested fraction of full-load torque (1.0 = full load). 0x0C3408 multiplies the same value by the Boost Limit to form the model's pressure AF8A (read). Rows: rpm. 0x0C4D84 (read): FFF8AFB4 = this(rpm, AFA8) in engine states 1/3/4; during cranking (FFF8906B = 2) FFF8AFB4 = FFF8AED6 instead. AFB4 goes through Throttle Opening (Required Area) in 0x0C326C to the commanded throttle FFF8AF84. The last column (AFA8 = 1.0) is 21468 = wide open in every row. At part throttle this table and Torque Fraction from Throttle Area cancel (one is the inverse of the other within interpolation), so the opening is set by the Throttle Opening from Target Torque tables. If you edit it at all, edit it with Torque Fraction from Throttle Area. The same data is also read as 05A15C. The monitor copy Throttle Required Area (Monitor) (05F3E8, data 0x049552) must be edited too. See my research notes. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05A148 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 008694. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Throttle Required Area (Monitor)
table.category: 04.03 Torque & Throttle - Throttle Control & Throttle Model
table.description:
Throttle-monitor copy of Throttle Required Area. Identical in stock; edit both together. Area is in mm^2 of effective throttle opening (about 2,150 mm^2 wide open).
Details: 0x185DD8 in the throttle monitor 0x186290 (read): separate copy (data 0x049552, axes 0x049A32/0x048F26) of Throttle Required Area 05A148, identical in stock. Edit together with 05A148. Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05F3E8 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00E570. Confidence: read.

table.name: Throttle Area from Opening
table.category: 04.03 Torque & Throttle - Throttle Control & Throttle Model
table.description:
Converts a throttle opening (%) into throttle area; the exact inverse of Throttle Opening (Required Area). Also gives the required area during cranking. Keep the two consistent; leave alone unless the throttle body changes. Area is in mm^2 of effective throttle opening (about 2,150 mm^2 wide open).
Details: 0x0BD5CC (read): FFF8AED6 = FFF8AE00 + this(FFF8AF12), FFF8ADFC = this(AF12). Its axis in % equals the Throttle Opening data and its data equals the Throttle Opening axis, point for point: it is the exact inverse of 05A0BC. table.name: Engine Torque from Load (DAM 1.0, TGV Closed)
table.description:
Engine torque the ECU expects at a given rpm and load; probably shapes the estimated/reported torque, not throttle or boost. This is the full-DAM set, for TGVs closed, no EGR (blended by TGV position and EGR amount). Stock EGR and non-EGR tables are identical.

They do not set the throttle or boost; they shape the estimated/reported engine torque (inferred). Axes: rpm FFF8CE9C x load % FFF8A616. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Full-Load Reference Brake Torque
table.description:
Full-load torque by rpm (density corrected) that the throttle/boost model divides every request by. It does not change part-throttle opening; it moves the full-load handover, target MAP and torque limits (raising it lowers target MAP for the same torque). Keep it equal to Throttle Opening Map Reference Torque from 2000 rpm, and edit the (Monitor) copy too.
Details: CORRECTION (end-to-end model, read arithmetic): at part throttle this table does NOT change the commanded opening (scaling it by 0.9 changes part-throttle opening by 0.00 %); it moves the full-load handover point and the target-MAP / torque-limit behaviour. Keep it equal to Throttle Opening Map Reference Torque (059DD0) from 2000 rpm, as stock. 0x0C2E70: scaled by FFF8AF52 = baro/101.3 kPa x 059F00(IAT) and added to 05A048 into FFF8AF64, the full-load indicated torque. The throttle opens in proportion to request / AF64, and target MAP = request/AF64 x boost ceiling (0x0C2F0C), so raising this table closes the throttle and lowers target MAP for the same torque. Stock 119-223 ft-lb (162-303 Nm); from 2000 rpm identical to 059DD0, the normaliser 0x0C0010 uses on the target torque. Part of the torque-to-throttle model; see my research notes (Phase 13). LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05A054 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 0085A0. Confidence: read.

table.name: Friction and Pumping Torque Loss
table.description:
Friction and pumping losses by rpm and manifold pressure, added to every torque request in the throttle/boost model. Cancels out at part throttle; matters near full load, for the torque estimate and limiters (raising it probably opens the throttle and raises target MAP). Edit the (Monitor) copy too.

table.name: Ignition Efficiency vs Retard
table.description:
How much torque the engine loses when timing is retarded from base timing (1.0 = no loss). table.name: Primary Ignition (TGV Closed, AVCS Active)
table.description:
Knock-limited ignition timing by rpm and load for TGVs closed while the cams are under AVCS control. With the knock correction advance and fine learning added it forms one side of the timing limit: the ECU fires the lower of this sum and the Base Timing map, and at high load in stock this side is the lower one, so it is effectively the WOT timing map.
Details: When used: Weight a (FFF84710) jumps to 255 when both cam controllers are in an active state (intake FFF8AB2C, exhaust FFF8AB1E = 1, 2, 6, or 9 with their bit 5) and falls by 8 per pass otherwise; forced to 0 while FFF88A2D bit 0 (engine stopped) is set (0x0D952C, read). So this table applies while AVCS is controlling. 0x0D952C (from 0x0DE0E0, read): Closed = 05B4A0 x a + 05B4B4 x (1 - a), Open = 05B4C8 x a + 05B4DC x (1 - a), result = Closed x (1 - TGV open fraction FFF8B3E8) + Open x FFF8B3E8, degrees = x/2 - 16, into FFF8A734 (closed blend) / FFF8A737 (open blend) / FFF8A736 (result), output FFF8A735 (optionally smoothed via FFF8C537 when FFF8AA85 bit 0 is set). FFF8A735 feeds the timing request (0x0E0A30 -> FFF8B10E -> FFF8A789) and so the spark target FFF8A72A, and FFF8A74A (0x0DA38C) (read). It sets the fired timing wherever it is the lower side of the timing limit (read, knock routing review 2026-10-31): 0x0E0A30 builds the pedal-pressed request FFF8A78A = this + coolant comp FFF8A787 + IAT comp FFF8A782 + EGR Timing Advance FFF8A769 (+ FFF8A77F / FFF8A786, neutral in stock); FFF8A789 adds the enrichment retard (0x0E0910); 0x0C13B4 compares FFF8A789 - 32 + 0.3516 deg x (KCA FFF8A791 + FLKC FFF8A7A7) with base timing FFF8A645, the shortfall becomes the efficiency FFF8AF22 (Ignition Efficiency vs Retard), and 0x0C39DC / 0x0DD568 turn it back into retard on FFF8A645 through the inverse table Torque Reduction Spark Retard. So the fired base FFF8A76A = min(Base Timing + comps, this + comps + EGR advance + KCA + FLKC) less torque-reduction retard (min() form computed), followed by tip-in retard, 0x0DD760, 0x0DA600 and the fired sum 0x0D9E40 (FBKC and retard terms). In stock at high load this table plus KCA is well below Base Timing (4000 rpm / 160 %, TGVs open, AVCS active: 3 degrees vs 21; computed), so this table with KCA and FLKC is effectively the wide-open-throttle timing. 0x0D9E40 uses FFF8A735 as the whole fired timing only when cal 0x239AE bit 1 is set (clear in stock), and in limit states FFF8A639 = 0x0B/0x0C/0x19/0x1A/0x1B the spark target FFF8A72A (0x0D9088, built from this request) replaces base timing outright (read). Weight a is a 0-255 ramp kept in FFF84710: +cal 0x2FFB0 (255) per pass while both cam controllers are active, -cal 0x2FFAF (8) per pass otherwise (0x0D952C, read). Axes rpm FFF8CE9C x load FFF8ADE4 (g/rev alternate). TGV polarity (read): 0x0D952C blends its Closed and Open ignition sets as Closed x (1 - FFF8B3E8) + Open x FFF8B3E8, so FFF8B3E8 is the TGV open fraction; 0x10C948 drives it toward 0 while FFF8A881 bit 4 is set, so that bit set = TGVs closed. p16 (read): 0x0D952C runs every 10 ms, so the weight falls 8 per 10 ms (full blend in about 0.32 s). LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05B4A0 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00A11C. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Volumetric Efficiency (TGV Closed)
table.category: 05.01 Airflow & Engine Model - Airflow / Load Model
table.description:
Volumetric efficiency by rpm and manifold pressure; feeds the ECU's air-mass model that defines engine load. The ECU blends the TGV Closed and TGV Open tables by actual TGV position. This is the TGVs-closed side. Retune when changing intake, cams or head flow.
Details: Volumetric efficiency, rpm x manifold pressure (psia). 0x11E280 blends Volumetric Efficiency (TGV Closed) x (1 - w) + Volumetric Efficiency (TGV Open) x w, with w = FFF8B3E8/65536 the TGV open fraction, into FFF8B4DA (read). 0x11E308 uses it (as VE = x/32768, rate-limited by cal 0x2B0E8/0x2B0EA). The exception is when cal 0x2C4D0 bit 0 is set (clear in stock) and FFF8A83B bit 7 is clear; then it uses Volumetric Efficiency (AVCS Not Ready, Off in Stock). The result FFF8C25C feeds the air-mass model whose output FFF8C250 defines engine load (0x0B7EFC). FFF8B3E8 comes from 0x10C948: the average of the two TGV position sensors FFF88AA6/88AA8 through 05D29C/05D290, ramped (cal 0x379EC/0x379EE) and gated by FFF8A881 bit 4 and FFF88E2A bit 5 (read). Polarity (read): 0x0D952C blends ignition as Closed x (1 - B3E8) + Open x B3E8, and 0x10C948 drives B3E8 toward 0 while FFF8A881 bit 4 (TGVs closed) is set. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05D8FC by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00C7A4. Confidence: inferred.

Details: Volumetric efficiency, rpm x manifold pressure (psia). 0x11E280 blends Volumetric Efficiency (TGV Closed) x (1 - w) + Volumetric Efficiency (TGV Open) x w, with w = FFF8B3E8/65536 the TGV open fraction, into FFF8B4DA (read). 0x11E308 uses it (as VE = x/32768, rate-limited by cal 0x2B0E8/0x2B0EA). The exception is when cal 0x2C4D0 bit 0 is set (clear in stock) and FFF8A83B bit 7 is clear; then it uses Volumetric Efficiency (AVCS Not Ready, Off in Stock). The result FFF8C25C feeds the air-mass model whose output FFF8C250 defines engine load (0x0B7EFC). FFF8B3E8 comes from 0x10C948: the average of the two TGV position sensors FFF88AA6/88AA8 through 05D29C/05D290, ramped (cal 0x379EC/0x379EE) and gated by FFF8A881 bit 4 and FFF88E2A bit 5 (read). Polarity (read): 0x0D952C blends ignition as Closed x (1 - B3E8) + Open x B3E8, and 0x10C948 drives B3E8 toward 0 while FFF8A881 bit 4 (TGVs closed) is set. table.category: 05.01 Airflow & Engine Model - Airflow / Load Model
table.description:

table.name: Throttle Area from Throttle Position (Airflow Model)
table.category: 05.01 Airflow & Engine Model - Airflow / Load Model
table.description:
Converts throttle position into effective throttle area (mm^2) for the airflow model and the throttle-based MAP substitute; about 2,150 mm^2 wide open. Stock it equals Throttle Area from Opening; for a different throttle body enter its measured open area here and in Throttle Area from Opening.

ADEC feeds the throttle flow of the manifold model (0x11D704: C24C = P_up/101325 x flow function x ADEC x temperature factor x cal, which corrects the pre-throttle pressure estimate toward the MAF, my research notes, read), the throttle-flow chain FFF8ADF8/ADF0 (Throttle Flow Curve (Area per RPM, MAP Fallback Model)) and FFF8A61F (its change per pass, 0x0B8A38) (read). Stock data are exactly 2 x Throttle Area from Opening at the same opening (read), so the scaling halves it into the area_raw unit (21468 = wide open). table.name: Throttle Flow Curve (Area per RPM, MAP Fallback Model)
table.category: 05.01 Airflow & Engine Model - Airflow / Load Model
table.description:
Airflow per revolution versus throttle area per rpm. Used for a throttle-based MAP substitute (probably when the MAP sensor is faulted) and as an input to transient (tip-in) fueling. Change only for a different throttle body.
Details: When used: always (0x0B8BB0 -> 0x0B8C74, read): FFF8ADF8 = rpm FFF8CD54 x this(FFF8ADEC x 1024 / CD54) / 32768, with ADEC from Throttle Area from Throttle Position; then 0x0B8980 forms FFF8ADF0 = ADF8 x 0.4/6e7 x cal 0x349C4 (14187) x FFF8CD46 x 0.0349 x 256 (filtered by cal 0x349C6), and when FFF88E28 bit 3 is set the MAP value FFF8913C becomes cal 0x58EA4 (52298) x ADF0 >> 15 instead of the sensor reading (0x1E0000 block, read): a throttle-based MAP substitute. table.name: Manifold Pressure Rate Span (RPM)
table.category: 05.01 Airflow & Engine Model - Airflow / Load Model
table.description:
How many samples (10 ms each) the ECU spans, by rpm, when measuring how fast manifold pressure is changing; that rate triggers the manifold model's transient corrections. Stock 7 samples at 800 rpm down to 2 from 5600 rpm.
Details: When used: every pass of 0x11CAB8 (from the airflow module, read). Seven MAP samples FFF88666 are kept in a delay line; FFF8B4CE = (MAP n passes ago - MAP now) / n x 3 (sign as coded; i.e. the negative MAP rate scaled to 3 passes), filtered with cal 0x2B9AC, where n = this(rpm FFF8CD54) clamped 1...7 (read). LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05D770 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00C618. Confidence: read.

table.name: Manifold Model Rising Transient Threshold
table.category: 05.01 Airflow & Engine Model - Airflow / Load Model
table.description:
How fast manifold pressure must rise (in gear) to count as a rising transient, which speeds up the ECU's manifold pressure model. Stock 4 kPa up to 90 kPa, 6 kPa at 105-150 kPa, 8 kPa from 165 kPa. Normally leave alone.

Rising transient: B4CA >= 05D7B8 (in gear) / 05D7C4 (neutral switch FFF88ADA b6 set), or a throttle step >= 05D80C (254, off). Falling transient: B4CA <= 05D7E8 (-6 kPa, hysteresis 05D7D0 +4 kPa) / 05D7F4 (-3 kPa, neutral). Output FFF8A8F9 multiplies the model gain FFF8B4D0 (0x11CC68: B4D0 is proportional to intake temperature x A8F9; 0x11D938 integrates R x B4D0 x (air in - air out) into the modelled pressure FFF8C238 when the model is active, FFF8A8FB b0 = running and rpm >= 100). A8F9 by phase: (1) rising transient and 1 pass after it (cal 0x2AF3B): 05D788(FFF8CDC2) = 179 in gear, cal 0x2C4C6 = 205 in neutral; (2) from the start of a falling transient for a duration from 05D8B8 / 05D890 / 05D8A4: the Initial table; (3) after that, until B4CA > cal 0x2BAD6 (-2 kPa): the Recovery table; (4) otherwise cal 0x2AF3E = 128. Initial/Recovery/duration values are sampled once at the start of the falling transient. Set: neutral switch -> Neutral tables; else TGV closed command FFF8A881 b4 -> TGV Closed tables; else the in-gear TGV-open tables. (For A8F9, 128 = x1.0, the steady-state gain; this table is a pressure threshold, not a gain.) This is the rising threshold in gear (hysteresis 05D7A0, 0). Stock 4 kPa (0.58 psi) up to 90 kPa, 6 kPa (0.87 psi) at 105-150 kPa, 8 kPa (1.16 psi) from 165 kPa. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05D7B8 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00C660. table.name: Manifold Model Start Correction RPM Threshold
table.category: 05.01 Airflow & Engine Model - Airflow / Load Model
table.description:
After start, once rpm passes this value (by coolant at start), the manifold model is pulled onto the MAF reading with the start gain (Manifold Model Start Correction MAF Gain) until model and MAF agree. Below this rpm the gain is 1.0. Stock 550 rpm cold down to 300 rpm from 70 C. Normally leave alone.
Details: Manifold-pressure model start phase 0x11C788 (10 ms task, read). Both tables are looked up with coolant at start FFF88A46 (the first stack argument; the disassembly shows R5 = EXTU.W @(40,R15) for 05D74C). FFF8C234 = 05D758 / 64 x 05D764(FFF8C540) / 128 while FFF8A8FC b6 is clear, else 1.0; b6 clears once rpm >= 05D74C x 6.25 after the model started (FFF8A8FB b0 rising) and stays clear until the modelled air FFF8C254 and the MAF value FFF88820/1280 agree within cal 0x2B999 x 0.2 (or FFF886AB b5 falls). C234 is the gain on the (MAF - model) term in 0x11DB50 (read), so the tables shape how fast the model is pulled onto the MAF after start (inferred). Stock 550 rpm up to 0 C (32 F), 544 / 525 / 494 rpm at 10 / 20 / 30 C, 400 at 40 C, 338 at 50 C, 306 at 60 C, 300 rpm from 70 C (158 F). LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05D74C by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00C5F4. Confidence: read.

table.name: Throttle Flow Coefficient (Forward Flow)
table.category: 05.01 Airflow & Engine Model - Airflow / Load Model
table.description:

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Map A (No Enrichment)
table.category: 05.02 Airflow & Engine Model - Exhaust & Temperature Models
table.description:
Exhaust temperature estimate (inferred) that decides when Primary Open Loop Fueling kicks in. Map A is the fast-reacting part, by rpm and load, used while no open loop enrichment is active. Raising it brings enrichment in earlier; lowering it delays it.
Details: When used: always while running. table.name: A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Base
table.category: 05.02 Airflow & Engine Model - Exhaust & Temperature Models
table.description:
Base exhaust temperature by rpm and load for the A/F sensor's exhaust model, which probably decides when it is safe to heat the front A/F sensor fully (water condensation check). Does not affect fuel or timing. Stock about 400-520 C at idle to about 1000 C at 6800 rpm.
Details: When used: always. 0x181334 (read): base exhaust temperature from rpm FFF8CD54 and load FFF8BAC4 (= FFF8ADE4, or cal 0x42E7E under FFF88E2A bit 1). Module 0x180C20 (read) is a self-contained exhaust thermal model: its result flags FFF8139F bit 0, which the A/F sensor state machine FFF88AFE reads (0x08492A / 0x0852B2, read); its role as the exhaust-pipe condensation check before full A/F sensor heating is inferred. 0x181334: T = this base x 05F208(final timing)/128 x (05F214(timing retard) + 128)/256 -> FFF8BAA8; FFF8BAC8 follows T with the 05F234 filter (towards coolant temperature while not running). No reader of FFF8BAC8 / FFF8BAA8 outside this module in the decompilation, so it does not affect fuel or timing (read). Stock 397-522 degC at 600 rpm, ~780 degC at 2400 rpm mid load, 975-1038 degC at 6800 rpm. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05F220 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00E3A8. Confidence: read.

table.name: A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Timing Factor
table.category: 05.02 Airflow & Engine Model - Exhaust & Temperature Models
table.description:
Correction of the A/F sensor exhaust temperature model for ignition timing (later timing = hotter exhaust). Does not affect fuel or timing. Stock 1.21 at -20 degrees to 1.0 from 15 degrees.
Details: When used: always. 0x181334 (read): multiplies the base exhaust temperature by this(final timing FFF8A744)/128. Both factors multiply the absolute temperature (base table + 223.15 K, i.e. Kelvin), not the degC/degF value shown: x1.10 on 800 C (1073 K) gives 907 C. table.name: A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Retard Factor

table.description:

table.name: A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Filter
table.category: 05.02 Airflow & Engine Model - Exhaust & Temperature Models
table.description:
How quickly the A/F sensor exhaust temperature model follows its target, by coolant. Does not affect fuel or timing. Normally leave alone.
Details: When used: always. 0x181334 (read): FFF8BAC8 = (previous x 32768 + target x k/2)/(32768 + k/2) with k = this(coolant FFF8CD65); target = the modelled exhaust temperature while running (engine state 3), else coolant temperature. table.name: A/F Sensor Exhaust Model Condensate at Start
table.category: 05.02 Airflow & Engine Model - Exhaust & Temperature Models
table.description:
Modelled water in the exhaust at start, by coolant and intake temperature. If it is above the threshold, full A/F sensor heating waits until the model has dried out. Raise to delay A/F sensor heating on cold starts, lower to allow it earlier.
Details: When used: at ignition on, at the cranking -> running change of FFF8906B, on rising FFF89053 bit 4 and while FFF89053 bit 3 is set (0x1801A4, read). Module 0x180C20 (read) is the exhaust condensation model behind the A/F sensor heater release: 05F158 (by pipe temperature FFF8BAB8, K x 32) is the saturation vapour pressure of water (stock 0.61 kPa at 0 C, 4.2 kPa at 30 C, 94 kPa at 98 C, in kPa x 8192 - read values); 0x17F4B8 takes the water partial pressure as cal 0x42333/256 (15 %) of max(MAP, baro) and makes the condensation rate FFF8C448 from flow x factor x (partial - saturation pressure) / total pressure; 0x18065C integrates the net amount into FFF8C48C. The A/F state machine (0x0852B2, read) goes to the protected state 2 when the start value FFF8C478 >= cal 0x4230C (415645) and on to state 3 only when FFF8139F bit 0 clears (0x08492A), which 0x181668 does when the model amount FFF8C47C < 415645. 0x1801A4 (read, args checked in the assembly): FFF8C478 = this(coolant FFF8AC8D, IAT FFF8AC8B; both degC + 50 bytes, cal 0x4234E / 0x42344 = -40 C on sensor fault) + FFF81880 (amount carried over from the last run). Above 415645 the A/F sensor heating waits for the model to dry out; below it the sensor takes the fast path (state 5). Stock 808794 at -30/-30 C, 415645 at 0/0 C (exactly the threshold), 0 from coolant 100 C or IAT 100 C. Raise to delay A/F sensor heating on cold starts, lower to allow it earlier. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05F1D0 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00E350. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: A/F Sensor Exhaust Model Condensation Flow Factor
table.category: 05.02 Airflow & Engine Model - Exhaust & Temperature Models
table.description:
Scales how fast water is modelled to condense in the exhaust, by exhaust flow (probably 1.0 = normal); more condensation keeps the front A/F sensor in its protected heating state longer. Normally leave alone.
Details: When used: always (module 0x180C20). Module 0x180C20 (read) is the exhaust condensation model behind the A/F sensor heater release: 05F158 (by pipe temperature FFF8BAB8, K x 32) is the saturation vapour pressure of water (stock 0.61 kPa at 0 C, 4.2 kPa at 30 C, 94 kPa at 98 C, in kPa x 8192 - read values); 0x17F4B8 takes the water partial pressure as cal 0x42333/256 (15 %) of max(MAP, baro) and makes the condensation rate FFF8C448 from flow x factor x (partial - saturation pressure) / total pressure; 0x18065C integrates the net amount into FFF8C48C. The A/F state machine (0x0852B2, read) goes to the protected state 2 when the start value FFF8C478 >= cal 0x4230C (415645) and on to state 3 only when FFF8139F bit 0 clears (0x08492A), which 0x181668 does when the model amount FFF8C47C < 415645. 0x180BE4 / 0x17F4B8 (read): the condensation rate FFF8C448 is proportional to this(exhaust flow FFF8C4B4) x FFF8C4B4 x cal 0x42DA8 x (water partial pressure - saturation pressure at pipe temperature) / total pressure, so this scales condensation linearly (256 = 1.0 assumed; inferred). Stock 0.80 from 0 to 20 g/s, rising to 1.21 at 61 g/s, 0.96 from 113 g/s. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05F1FC by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00E384. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: A/F Sensor Exhaust Model Saturation Vapour Pressure
table.category: 05.02 Airflow & Engine Model - Exhaust & Temperature Models
table.description:
Water vapour pressure versus exhaust pipe temperature for the A/F sensor condensation model, which decides how long the front A/F sensor is kept in protected heating. Stock is the real physical curve; leave alone.
Details: When used: always (exhaust condensation model 0x180C20 behind the A/F sensor heater release, read). 0x17F4B8 (read; axis = pipe temperature FFF8BAB8, LF75404S_table_inputs): saturation = this(pipe temperature); total pressure = max(MAP, baro) in kPa x 8192; water partial pressure = total x cal 0x42333/256 (15 %); the condensation rate FFF8C448 = flow FFF8C4B4 x Condensation Flow Factor x cal 0x42DA8 x (partial - saturation) / total, clamped >= 0, and is integrated (minus evaporation) into the condensate amount that holds the A/F sensor in its protected heating state (see A/F Sensor Exhaust Model Condensate at Start). Stock is the physical saturation vapour pressure of water: 0.61 kPa at 0 C, 4.25 kPa at 30 C, 95 kPa at 98 C, 1509 kPa at 196 C; the last point (899 C) is 4294946604 (near the u32 maximum), so above 196 C no condensation is possible. Raising the curve lowers the modelled condensation (shorter heater protection), lowering it lengthens it; the physics argues for leaving it. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05F158 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00E2D8. Confidence: read.

table.name: A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Hot Restart Factor (2D)
table.category: 05.02 Airflow & Engine Model - Exhaust & Temperature Models
table.description:
2017+ / Forester version of A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Hot Restart Factor: on a hot restart the exhaust model starts from the stored pipe temperature times this factor, by stored temperature and coolant drop. Stock 1.0 at no drop to 0.7 at 30 C drop, the same for every stored temperature. Normally leave alone.
Details: When used: before the engine runs, on a hot restart: coolant at start high enough (cals 0x4B638/0x4B639 = 10/110, i.e. the same >= 60 C, 50 C to stay test as LF75404S cals 0x4234C/D) and last running coolant FFF8069B >= cal 0x4B63B (130 = 80 C). 2017+/Forester replacement of the LF75404S 1D table A/F Sensor Exhaust Temp Model Hot Restart Factor (05F1E4), which these images do not have. LF79002P 0x1866D8 (counterpart of LF75404S 0x1802F4; stack arguments checked in the LF79002P disassembly: param_9 @72 = FFF81678, called at 0x18716A, read): the modelled exhaust pipe temperature (K x 32) starts at max(FFF81678 x this(FFF81678, coolant drop)/256, min(IAT, coolant) (C150/C152)). FFF81678 is the pipe temperature latched when the engine stops (0x1866B8, read; = LF75404S FFF815BA). Axis 1 = that stored pipe temperature (u16, K x 32; the lookup 0x1B0D7C clamps it and the drop to the axis ends), axis 2 = the coolant drop since the engine last ran, FFF8069B - FFF88D96 x 160/65536 - 10 (s8, degC) (read). Data u8, unsigned interpolation in 0x1B0D7C, layout [stored-temperature index x 8 + drop index] (read). The starting temperature drives the exhaust condensation model behind the A/F sensor heater release (see A/F Sensor Exhaust Model Saturation Vapour Pressure). Stock identical in all four images and in every row (no dependence on the stored temperature): 1.00 (255) at 0 C drop, 0.95 at 5, 0.90 at 10, 0.85 at 15, 0.80 at 20, 0.75 at 25, 0.70 at 30 and 35 C drop - the same curve as LF75404S 05F1E4, with 5 C steps. LF9C100P: a table LF75404S does not have. Evidence: Phase 19 group X (my research notes): reader 0x183B20, call site 183BD8; replaces the 1D hot-restart factor of the 2015 code (read). Descriptor 00E370. Confidence: read.

table.name: Exhaust Temperature Model Map A Enrichment Adder (Zero in Stock)
table.category: 05.02 Airflow & Engine Model - Exhaust & Temperature Models
table.description:
2017+ only: extra amount added to Exhaust Temperature Model Map A (Enriched) while open loop enrichment is active, scaled by how far the enrichment has progressed (inferred). All zero in stock, so it has no effect until filled.
Details: When used: while open-loop enrichment is active (FFF8ABF4 != 0). 2017+ only. The LF79002P exhaust temperature model adds a signed term in the enriched branch (read, LF79002P decompilation): value = enriched map x retard multiplier / 256 + FFF8ABEE x this(rpm FFF8D3D4, load FFF8AB76)/256. FFF8ABEE = (enrichment FFF8ABF4 - FFF8ABF5) x 256 / (FFF8ABED - FFF8ABF5), clamped 0..255 (0x0DFB18, read), where FFF8ABED comes from 0x0DFA88, the Primary Open Loop Fueling style lookup on the 24 x 20 open-loop grid (0655F8 + 065620 x 065640(DAM) - 065634 x 06560C) - i.e. how far the enrichment has come towards the open-loop target (inferred). The table uses that same 24 x 20 grid (400-9200 rpm x 0.91-2.97 g/rev (70-230 % load)). All zero in LF79002P, LF79100P and LF9C100P (read), so the term has no effect in stock. Same data address in all three images; descriptors placed from the call sites (LF79100P / LF9C100P callsite maps and decompilations, read). LF79002P 0x0D9F80 (counterpart of LF75404S 0x0C9878): added to S = Exhaust Temperature Model Map A (Enriched) 064D64 x Retard Multiplier A (Enriched) 064E78 / 256 (unless FFF8AE27 bit 4 selects the Standstill High Load map). table.name: Intake Cam Target 1A (TGV Open, Normal, Altitude)
table.description:
Intake cam advance target (degrees from the fully retarded rest position) by rpm and load for normal driving with the TGVs open, used at altitude (blended in by AVCS Barometric Blend; near sea level the 1B table is used instead). Higher = earlier intake valve timing. The normal vs high-pedal split is inferred from the switching conditions.
Details: Convention (read, see FU_UNITS): crank degrees of intake cam ADVANCE from its learned rest position; 0 = rest (fully retarded, inferred), larger = more advance (earlier valve events). Values below 0 ask for less than the rest position: the OCV then sits at minimum duty and the cam stays at rest (inferred). AVCS target (intake 0x15C250, exhaust 0x16032C, read): target = coolant terms + v x [S_A x w + S_B x (1 - w)] + (1 - v) x [3A x w + (3B + Coolant Offset 3B x Coolant Factor 3 / 128) x (1 - w)], clamped to +/-90 degrees, 364.09 counts per degree. v = FFF8B3E8, the TGV open fraction: sets 1/2 apply with TGVs open, set 3 with TGVs closed. w = FFF8B948 = AVCS Barometric Blend (barometric pressure FFF88668, via 0x15B1E0, read): the A tables apply at altitude, the B tables at sea level.
