table.description:
How long after every start the cams are held at their rest position before cam control begins, by coolant temperature at start. Stock is 10 s below -20 degC, 2.8 s when warm and 3.7 s when hot. Raise for a longer hold, lower to start cam control sooner.
Details: When used: after every start. 0x15B59C (intake) and 0x15F7C0 (exhaust, descriptor 05E770, same data 0x03AD6A) (read): while FFF88A76 / 2 is below this(coolant at start FFF88A46) the AVCS request FFF8AB2D / FFF8AB1F is 4 (hold at the default position, no closed-loop cam control). FFF88A76 counts 10 ms passes since the engine left cranking (0x07E1AC: +1 per call, saturating at 65535, reset while FFF88A27 bit 0 is set; called once per pass from 0x07D3E4 in the 10 ms task 0x1DFE3C, read), so one table count = 20 ms. Stock 10 s (raw 500) below -20 degC, 8 s at -10, 5 s at 0, 3.5 s at 10, 2.8 s at 20-60 degC, 3.7 s from 70 degC. A second table (05E414) can only shorten it once the delay has run out (read), which has no effect in stock (inferred). LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05E408 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00D394. Confidence: read.

table.name: AVCS Minimum Oil Temp (IAT at Start)
table.description:
Minimum oil temperature before cam control is allowed, by intake air temperature at start (a proxy for how cold the engine was). Below it the cams stay at rest. Stock: 80 degC oil after a -40 degC start, 25 degC after a 0 degC start, no limit from 5 degC up.
Details: When used: always. 0x15B59C (intake) and 0x15F7C0 (exhaust, descriptor 05E788, same data 0x03AD8A) (read): the active-control request (FFF8AB2D = 1) needs oil temperature FFF8B97C >= this(FFF8CEE6) plus the rpm / pedal windows; otherwise the request is 9 (FFF8AB28 bit 5 / FFF8AB24 bit 5 clear). FFF8CEE6 = intake air temperature latched at start, (IAT + 50 - 10) x 65536/160 (0x06AF58, read), the iat_409 scale. Stock 80 degC oil for a start at -40 degC, 25 degC at 0 degC, no limit from 5 degC up. FFF8B97C is oil temperature: 0x15B1E0 writes it from FFF88E26 (oil temperature, OBD PID 0x5C units) because cal 0x3ACF1 = 1, or from coolant FFF88A44 x 32/41 (the same scale) when that cal is 0 (read). Earlier notes called FFF8B97C battery voltage; that is wrong. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05E42C by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00D3B8. Confidence: read.

table.name: Intake AVCS Fixed Duty Window After Start
table.description:
Appears to set how long after a start (by coolant at start) the intake cam valves are held at a fixed 52 % duty instead of closed-loop control. Only matters if longer than AVCS Activation Delay After Start; in stock it never is, so it probably has no effect on a stock car.
Details: When used: every pass while running; only matters if it is longer than AVCS Activation Delay After Start. Time after start (A76/2, 20 ms counts) during which the intake OCV duty is held at the fixed 52 % (cal 0x3CE52) instead of closed-loop cam control, when the oil-temperature condition (Intake AVCS Fixed Duty Minimum Oil Temp) also holds. Stock 10 s at -40..-20 degC coolant at start, 8 s at -10, 5 s at 0, 3.5 s at 10, 2.8 s at 20-50, 2 s from 60 degC; this is never longer than AVCS Activation Delay After Start (equal up to 50 degC, shorter from 60 degC), so in stock the window ends before closed-loop control starts (inferred). Its own data block (0x3D066), not the one of AVCS Activation Delay After Start (Second, Unused) (0x3D088); the two hold the same stock values (read). 0x15B59C (intake AVCS request, read; arguments mapped from the call at seg_0x150000.c:7959 and the stack offsets at 0x15B5BC-0x15B68C): 05E420 and 05E414 / 05E408 are read with coolant at start FFF88A46 (R14 at 0x15B664-0x15B674), 05E42C and 05E438 with IAT at start FFF8CEE6 (R12 at 0x15B678-0x15B68C). Output FFF8AB2A bit 3 = 1 unless all of: AVCS enable status FFF8AB2E = 0, FFF88ADA bit 3 clear, FFF8AB27 bit 6 clear, not (rpm CE9C <= cal 0x3AD38 = 450 rpm with FFF88A28 bit 1) and FFF88A76/2 >= Fixed Duty Window. Output FFF8AB2A bit 4 = (Fixed Duty Minimum Oil Temp(IAT at start) <= oil FFF8B97C x 328 >> 16) and FFF8AB28 bit 7 and FFF8AB27 bit 5 and the rpm/angle windows of cals 0x3AD1A-0x3AD46 (same structure as AVCS Minimum Oil Temp (IAT at Start), which sets FFF8AB28 bit 5). In 0x15DF20 (cam 1) and 0x15E63C (cam 2), when both bits are set the duty B8DE is not feedback + hold but max(min(cal 0x3B8FE, cal 0x3CE52), cal 0x3B8FC) = 1300 = 52 % (read); B8DE becomes the OCV output B8EA only in AVCS states 1/6 (FFF8AB28 bit 3, slice D). LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05E420 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00D3AC. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Intake AVCS Fixed Duty Minimum Oil Temp (IAT at Start)
table.description:
Appears to set the oil temperature, by intake air temperature at start, above which the intake cam valves are held at a fixed 52 % duty during Intake AVCS Fixed Duty Window After Start instead of closed-loop control. Stock 79 degC after a very cold start, no limit from 5 degC up. Only acts during Intake AVCS Fixed Duty Window After Start, which in stock ends before cam control starts, so it probably has no effect on a stock car.
Details: When used: every pass while running. Oil temperature above which the intake fixed-duty hold (52 %, cal 0x3CE52) may apply during Intake AVCS Fixed Duty Window After Start, by IAT at start. Stock 79 degC at IAT -40..-20 degC, 54 degC at -10, 44 at -5, 24 at 0, 0 degC (no limit, byte 64) from +5 degC; close to AVCS Minimum Oil Temp (IAT at Start) except at IAT -20 degC (79 vs 70 degC). 0x15B59C (intake AVCS request, read; arguments mapped from the call at seg_0x150000.c:7959 and the stack offsets at 0x15B5BC-0x15B68C): 05E420 and 05E414 / 05E408 are read with coolant at start FFF88A46 (R14 at 0x15B664-0x15B674), 05E42C and 05E438 with IAT at start FFF8CEE6 (R12 at 0x15B678-0x15B68C). Output FFF8AB2A bit 3 = 1 unless all of: AVCS enable status FFF8AB2E = 0, FFF88ADA bit 3 clear, FFF8AB27 bit 6 clear, not (rpm CE9C <= cal 0x3AD38 = 450 rpm with FFF88A28 bit 1) and FFF88A76/2 >= Fixed Duty Window. Output FFF8AB2A bit 4 = (Fixed Duty Minimum Oil Temp(IAT at start) <= oil FFF8B97C x 328 >> 16) and FFF8AB28 bit 7 and FFF8AB27 bit 5 and the rpm/angle windows of cals 0x3AD1A-0x3AD46 (same structure as AVCS Minimum Oil Temp (IAT at Start), which sets FFF8AB28 bit 5). In 0x15DF20 (cam 1) and 0x15E63C (cam 2), when both bits are set the duty B8DE is not feedback + hold but max(min(cal 0x3B8FE, cal 0x3CE52), cal 0x3B8FC) = 1300 = 52 % (read); B8DE becomes the OCV output B8EA only in AVCS states 1/6 (FFF8AB28 bit 3, slice D). LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05E438 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00D3C4. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Intake AVCS Feedback Duty (Idle, Cam 1)
table.description:
Proportional part of the intake cam 1 oil control valve duty by rpm and cam error, used with the pedal fully released and the car below about 4 km/h; otherwise Intake AVCS Feedback Duty (Cam 1) is used. Stock about -9.5 % to +8 % at the error extremes, 0 at zero error.
Details: Axis (read, see FU_UNITS): cam error = target - actual in crank degrees (intake: advance, exhaust: retard); positive error = the cam must move away from its rest position, and stock duty rises with it. When used: intake cam 1 (0x15DF20, error FFF8B956) at idle / standstill. This is the idle variant, used while the accelerator is fully released (FFF88C64 bit 5) and vehicle speed FFF88BE8 x 9/160 < cal 0x3B904 (4 km/h); otherwise Intake AVCS Feedback Duty (Cam 1) is used. 0x15DF20 / 0x15E63C (intake cam 1 / cam 2) and 0x16269C / 0x162D18 (exhaust cam 1 / cam 2), read: duty = learned hold duty (FFF8B8E8 / FFF8B8E6 intake cam 1 / 2, FFF8B8FE / FFF8B8FC exhaust cam 1 / 2) + (P + D) x cal 0x3B90C/100 (exhaust cal 0x3C7E2; both 100 %), clamped 31.9...81.1 % (exhaust 32.1...81.1 %). P = this table (-100 + x/327.68 %) x oil factor/128, used when the cam error (intake FFF8B956 / B954 from 0x15CF8C, exhaust FFF8B916 / B914 from 0x16168C; target - actual) exceeds 0.5 deg (cal 0x3B90A intake, 0x3C7E0 exhaust). The feedback duty is the output only in the active states 1/6 (FFF8AB28 bit 3 intake, FFF8AB24 bit 3 exhaust). Stock -4.5...-9.5 % at -40 deg error, +3.5...+8 % at +40 deg, 0 at 0. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05E5CC by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00D638. Confidence: read.

The feedback duty is the output only in the active states 1/6 (FFF8AB28 bit 3 intake, FFF8AB24 bit 3 exhaust). Stock -8...-9.2 % at -40 deg error, +6.5...+7.5 % at +40 deg. table.name: Intake AVCS Rate Feedback Duty (Cam 1)
table.description:
Damping (derivative) part of the intake cam 1 oil control valve duty by rpm and how fast the cam error is changing, added to the proportional term during active cam control. Stock only acts at 700 rpm, and Intake AVCS Rate Feedback Oil Factor turns it off from 80 degC oil.
Details: When used: intake cam 1 in active control (0x15DF20). D term (read): when |FFF8B952| (the filtered rate of change of the cam error, 0x15CF8C) exceeds 0.5 deg (cal 0x3CCC8), D = (-100 + this(rpm, rate)/327.68 %) x oil factor/128 x 05E5F4(error)/128 (128 = 1.0 in stock), added to the P term. Oil factor Intake AVCS Rate Feedback Oil Factor (05E590). Stock -10 % / +3 % at the extreme rates at 700 rpm only, 0 elsewhere. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05E600 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00D66C. Confidence: read.

table.name: Intake AVCS OCV Battery Voltage Compensation
table.description:
Multiplier on both intake oil control valve outputs by battery voltage, so the valves get the same effective drive as voltage changes. Always used. Stock 1.40 at 10 V, 1.0 at 14 V, 0.875 at 16 V.
Details: When used: always, both intake OCVs (0x15ED58; descriptor 05E6E0 in 0x15F158, same data 0x03BC84). 0x15ED58 / 0x15F158 (intake cam 1 / 2) and 0x163394 / 0x163788 (exhaust cam 1 / 2), read: OCV output = (I term + duty FFF8B8EA x coil factor x adaptation factor) x battery factor, stored x25 into FFF8B8EE (intake cam 1). The adaptation factor (0.5...1.5, cal 0x3BBCE/0x3BBCC) is stepped by the current error = expected current (Expected Current table) - measured FFF88D70 x 2.5/65536 while the duty is >= 20 % (cal 0x3BBC4). The battery factor is this(FFF88C9E, filtered battery voltage). Stock 14 V / V: 1.40 at 10 V, 1.0 at 14 V, 0.875 at 16 V. The exhaust OCVs use Exhaust AVCS OCV Battery Voltage Compensation (05E9C8). LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05E698 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00D704. Confidence: read.

table.name: Post-Start Idle Air (Initial)
table.description:

table.name: Minimum Idle Air (Moving in Gear)
table.description:
Floor on idle air by rpm (and coolant) whenever the car is moving in gear, so the throttle cannot close below it; acts mainly as a dashpot when the pedal is released (inferred). Raise to soften throttle closing on decel; lower for faster rpm drop. Not used at standstill or in neutral.

Stock 3840 at 0 rpm, 2816 at 400-800 rpm, 4608 at 1600 (cold; 2944 at 1200 and 3840 at 1600 rpm from 80 degC), 5632 at 2000, 8192 at 2800, 13184 at 4000, 16384 at 4400, 20480 at 5600 and 22016 from 6400 rpm; otherwise independent of coolant. table.name: TGV Torque Threshold Enter (Drive Modes 1/4, Default/Sport Sharp)

table.name: Cruise Maximum Speed (km/h Meter)
table.description:
Upper cruise speed by meter (market) code; the name 'maximum cruise speed' is inferred from the values. table.name: Cruise Speed Error Gain (State 0x23)
table.description:
Cruise controller gain by acceleration and speed error used after a short tap of the raise (accelerate) switch (tap meaning inferred). Higher = more aggressive throttle response. Stock mostly small gains.
Details: Cruise module 0x165AC4/0x1663AC, 20 ms task (read). Cruise runs on this 6MT ROM: cal 0x57788 = 0x03 enables the analog steering-switch input FFF88E76 (0x08DF14: main switch -> FFF88EC9 b6; two momentary switches -> FFF88EC9 b1 (raises the set speed) and b0 (lowers it), read; 'accelerate'/'coast' are inferred names); no MT-coding gate was found. 0x16AF7C (read): the cruise speed controller multiplies the speed error (target FFF8B9DC - speed FFF8B9F4) by a gain from one of seven tables, selected by the cruise state FFF8AB58 (state machine 0x168AC2) and flags: AB3D b0/b1 -> 05EE58; else state 0x23 -> 05EE1C; state 0xB0 -> 05EE44; state 0xC0, or any other state while the speed is not within 2 km/h of the maximum cruise speed FFF8B9F0 (86B5F): AB42 b2 -> 05EE94, else state 0x40 -> 05EE80, state 0xC0 -> 05EE6C; otherwise (incl. the hold state 0x33) -> 05EE30. Axes: vehicle acceleration FFF8B9C2 and speed error. The gain x 05EED0-family(rpm)/160 is filtered into FFF8C5BE, which is integrated with the error into the drive-torque command FFF8C438 -> FFF8B9E2. State 0x23 is entered from states 1/2 when FFF88E11 b4 is set (a short press of the raise switch, 0x16D068, read): an accelerate tap (inferred). Stock 16-96 in most cells, 83-88 from 6 km/h/s, and 1920 / 480 at +5 / +5.5 km/h error with acceleration up to 0.7 km/h/s. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05EE1C by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00DF70. Confidence: inferred.

The gain x 05EED0-family(rpm)/160 is filtered into FFF8C5BE, which is integrated with the error into the drive-torque command FFF8C438 -> FFF8B9E2. State 0xB0 is entered from states 0xCF/0xC0 when FFF88E11 b6 is set (a short press of the lowering switch, 0x16EC04, read): a coast tap (inferred). Stock 640 everywhere except 0 at zero speed error. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05EE44 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00DF98. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Cruise Speed Error Gain (Catch-Up)
table.description:
Cruise controller gain by acceleration and speed error, used while the car catches up to a set speed changed by holding a switch (inferred). Higher = more aggressive throttle response.
Details: Cruise module 0x165AC4/0x1663AC, 20 ms task (read). Cruise runs on this 6MT ROM: cal 0x57788 = 0x03 enables the analog steering-switch input FFF88E76 (0x08DF14: main switch -> FFF88EC9 b6; two momentary switches -> FFF88EC9 b1 (raises the set speed) and b0 (lowers it), read; 'accelerate'/'coast' are inferred names); no MT-coding gate was found. 0x16AF7C (read): the cruise speed controller multiplies the speed error (target FFF8B9DC - speed FFF8B9F4) by a gain from one of seven tables, selected by the cruise state FFF8AB58 (state machine 0x168AC2) and flags: AB3D b0/b1 -> 05EE58; else state 0x23 -> 05EE1C; state 0xB0 -> 05EE44; state 0xC0, or any other state while the speed is not within 2 km/h of the maximum cruise speed FFF8B9F0 (86B5F): AB42 b2 -> 05EE94, else state 0x40 -> 05EE80, state 0xC0 -> 05EE6C; otherwise (incl. the hold state 0x33) -> 05EE30. Axes: vehicle acceleration FFF8B9C2 and speed error. The gain x 05EED0-family(rpm)/160 is filtered into FFF8C5BE, which is integrated with the error into the drive-torque command FFF8C438 -> FFF8B9E2. Used whenever FFF8AB3D b0 or b1 is set (overrides the state): b0 (0x16FB58) is set by FFF88E11 b5 and held until the set speed FFF8B9FA - speed < cal 0x418E0 (3 km/h); b1 (0x16FA9C) by FFF88E11 b7 until speed - set speed < cal 0x418DE (read), i.e. while the car catches up with a set speed changed by a held switch (inferred). Stock 16-272 in most cells, 1920 / 480 at +5 / +6 km/h error while decelerating by 1.5 km/h/s or more. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05EE58 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00DFAC. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Cruise Speed Error Gain (State 0x40)
table.description:
Cruise controller gain by acceleration and speed error used after the raise switch, while not within 2 km/h of the maximum cruise speed. Higher = more aggressive throttle response. Stock 96, higher for small errors at low acceleration.
Details: Cruise module 0x165AC4/0x1663AC, 20 ms task (read). Cruise runs on this 6MT ROM: cal 0x57788 = 0x03 enables the analog steering-switch input FFF88E76 (0x08DF14: main switch -> FFF88EC9 b6; two momentary switches -> FFF88EC9 b1 (raises the set speed) and b0 (lowers it), read; 'accelerate'/'coast' are inferred names); no MT-coding gate was found. 0x16AF7C (read): the cruise speed controller multiplies the speed error (target FFF8B9DC - speed FFF8B9F4) by a gain from one of seven tables, selected by the cruise state FFF8AB58 (state machine 0x168AC2) and flags: AB3D b0/b1 -> 05EE58; else state 0x23 -> 05EE1C; state 0xB0 -> 05EE44; state 0xC0, or any other state while the speed is not within 2 km/h of the maximum cruise speed FFF8B9F0 (86B5F): AB42 b2 -> 05EE94, else state 0x40 -> 05EE80, state 0xC0 -> 05EE6C; otherwise (incl. the hold state 0x33) -> 05EE30. Axes: vehicle acceleration FFF8B9C2 and speed error. The gain x 05EED0-family(rpm)/160 is filtered into FFF8C5BE, which is integrated with the error into the drive-torque command FFF8C438 -> FFF8B9E2. State 0x40 is entered on FFF8AB3F b5 (0x17039C, from the raise switch FFF88EC9 b1); used only while the speed is not within 2 km/h of the maximum cruise speed. Stock 96, with 491-2560 for small positive errors (0.5-2.6 km/h) at acceleration <= 0.3 km/h/s. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05EE80 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00DFD4. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Cruise Speed Error Gain (Set-Speed Approach)
table.description:
Cruise controller gain by acceleration and speed error while approaching a new set speed, until within about 3 km/h of it. Stock high for small errors at low acceleration, small elsewhere.
Details: Cruise module 0x165AC4/0x1663AC, 20 ms task (read). Cruise runs on this 6MT ROM: cal 0x57788 = 0x03 enables the analog steering-switch input FFF88E76 (0x08DF14: main switch -> FFF88EC9 b6; two momentary switches -> FFF88EC9 b1 (raises the set speed) and b0 (lowers it), read; 'accelerate'/'coast' are inferred names); no MT-coding gate was found. 0x16AF7C (read): the cruise speed controller multiplies the speed error (target FFF8B9DC - speed FFF8B9F4) by a gain from one of seven tables, selected by the cruise state FFF8AB58 (state machine 0x168AC2) and flags: AB3D b0/b1 -> 05EE58; else state 0x23 -> 05EE1C; state 0xB0 -> 05EE44; state 0xC0, or any other state while the speed is not within 2 km/h of the maximum cruise speed FFF8B9F0 (86B5F): AB42 b2 -> 05EE94, else state 0x40 -> 05EE80, state 0xC0 -> 05EE6C; otherwise (incl. the hold state 0x33) -> 05EE30. Axes: vehicle acceleration FFF8B9C2 and speed error. The gain x 05EED0-family(rpm)/160 is filtered into FFF8C5BE, which is integrated with the error into the drive-torque command FFF8C438 -> FFF8B9E2. Used in states 0x40 / 0xC0 (or away from the maximum speed) while FFF8AB42 b2 is set (0x1705D0: set by FFF8AB3F b3 or b5, cleared when |set speed FFF8B9FA - speed| <= cal 0x418E4 = 3 km/h, read). Stock 1551-4195 for errors up to 1 km/h at accelerations up to 0.5 km/h/s, 48-240 elsewhere below 1.5 km/h/s, 1-59 from 1.5 km/h/s (the axis covers positive errors only: car slower than target). LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05EE94 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00DFE8. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Cruise Integrator Preset (Engage)
table.description:
Value the cruise controller's integral term is preset to when cruise starts controlling or returns to holding speed, by speed and acceleration. Stock nonzero only for gentle deceleration, larger at higher speed.
Details: Cruise module 0x165AC4/0x1663AC, 20 ms task (read). Cruise runs on this 6MT ROM: cal 0x57788 = 0x03 enables the analog steering-switch input FFF88E76 (0x08DF14: main switch -> FFF88EC9 b6; two momentary switches -> FFF88EC9 b1 (raises the set speed) and b0 (lowers it), read; 'accelerate'/'coast' are inferred names); no MT-coding gate was found. 0x16AF7C (read): the controller integrator FFF86B48 is preset to (feed-forward + this(speed FFF8B9F4, acceleration FFF8B9C2) x 0.025) / 2 on the pass cruise control starts controlling (FFF8AB40 b5 rising) and on the change from state 0xCF to the hold state 0x33. Stock nonzero only for accelerations -2.0 to -0.2 km/h/s (gentle deceleration): 100 at 20 km/h rising to 500 from 140 km/h (raw 4000 to 20000; the table shows raw x 0.025); 0 elsewhere. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05EEA8 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00DFFC. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Cruise Integrator Preset (After Tap)
table.description:
Value the cruise controller's integral term is preset to after a set-speed switch tap, by speed and acceleration, so speed settles smoothly. Stock positive when decelerating, negative when accelerating, 0 near steady speed.
Details: Cruise module 0x165AC4/0x1663AC, 20 ms task (read). Cruise runs on this 6MT ROM: cal 0x57788 = 0x03 enables the analog steering-switch input FFF88E76 (0x08DF14: main switch -> FFF88EC9 b6; two momentary switches -> FFF88EC9 b1 (raises the set speed) and b0 (lowers it), read; 'accelerate'/'coast' are inferred names); no MT-coding gate was found. 0x16AF7C (read): the controller integrator FFF86B48 is preset to (feed-forward + this(speed FFF8B9F4, acceleration FFF8B9C2) x 0.025) / 2 on the change from state 0x23 to 0x33 (enabled by cal 0x3F850 b3 = 1) and from 0xB0 to 0x33 (cal 0x3F850 b4 = 1). Stock +450 to +800 when decelerating (<= -1.5 km/h/s), 0 within +/-0.5 km/h/s, -400 to -600 when accelerating (>= 1.5 km/h/s) (raw +18000 to +32000 and -16000 to -24000; the table shows raw x 0.025). LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05EEBC by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00E010. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Cruise Vehicle Speed from CAN Speed
table.description:
Converts the CAN vehicle speed into the speed used by cruise control, per meter (market) code, as a straight line (scale and offset). The offsets probably make the set speed match the speedometer. Stock 1.0 x speed for most codes, up to 1.048 x + 1.8 km/h.
Details: Cruise module 0x165AC4/0x1663AC, 20 ms task (read). Cruise runs on this 6MT ROM: cal 0x57788 = 0x03 enables the analog steering-switch input FFF88E76 (0x08DF14: main switch -> FFF88EC9 b6; two momentary switches -> FFF88EC9 b1 (raises the set speed) and b0 (lowers it), read; 'accelerate'/'coast' are inferred names); no MT-coding gate was found. 0x16C2D0 (read): while FFF88E28 b0 and the VDC CAN fault FFF88BF9 b0 are clear and FFF88B94 b2 is set, the cruise speed FFF8B9F4 = filter(this(meter code FFF8A88C, CAN speed FFF8B4C2), weight 05F054); otherwise B9F4 = cal 0x4073C (10 km/h). The column axis is 0 and 5333 (300 km/h) followed by 14 points just above 300 km/h (5334-5347) holding the same values, so each row is a straight line: speed x k + offset (edit columns 2-16 together). Stock row 0 (and 7, 10, 11, 13-15) = 1.000 x speed; row 1 1.048 x + 1.8 km/h; rows 2/3 0.997 x + 1.0 km/h; rows 4-6, 8, 12 1.036 x + 1.9 km/h; row 9 1.016 x + 2.7 km/h. The row offsets look like speedometer corrections so the set speed matches the meter (inferred). Above 300 km/h the last column holds. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05F040 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00E194. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Cruise Vehicle Speed Filter Weight
table.description:
Smoothing weight for the vehicle speed used by cruise control, by speed error and speed. Larger = less smoothing, quicker reaction. Stock 0.3 at zero error up to 0.8 at 0.4 km/h error; 0.25 at 200 km/h.
Details: Cruise module 0x165AC4/0x1663AC, 20 ms task (read). Cruise runs on this 6MT ROM: cal 0x57788 = 0x03 enables the analog steering-switch input FFF88E76 (0x08DF14: main switch -> FFF88EC9 b6; two momentary switches -> FFF88EC9 b1 (raises the set speed) and b0 (lowers it), read; 'accelerate'/'coast' are inferred names); no MT-coding gate was found. 0x16C2D0 (read): first-order filter (0x6CEC) of 05F040's output into FFF8B9F4 with this weight. Axis 1 = FFF8B9C4 = speed - cruise target while cruise is controlling, else 0 (0x1693D8, read; shown in km/h); axis 2 = the previous filtered speed. Stock 0.30 at zero error, 0.40 at +/-0.2 km/h, 0.80 at +/-0.4 km/h (0.40 at 150 km/h); 0.25 everywhere at 200 km/h. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05F054 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00E1BC. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Cruise Excess Acceleration Threshold (Meter Cruise Option, Alternate)
table.description:
With one cruise option and an alternate flag only: if the car accelerates faster than this (by speed) for 0.2 s while cruise is on without pedal input, cruise ends (probably a runaway check). Stock 21.6 km/h/s up to 40 km/h, 10.8 km/h/s at 80 km/h.
Details: Cruise module 0x165AC4/0x1663AC, 20 ms task (read). Cruise runs on this 6MT ROM: cal 0x57788 = 0x03 enables the analog steering-switch input FFF88E76 (0x08DF14: main switch -> FFF88EC9 b6; two momentary switches -> FFF88EC9 b1 (raises the set speed) and b0 (lowers it), read; 'accelerate'/'coast' are inferred names); no MT-coding gate was found. 0x16E6EC (read): used only while FFF811E1 b4 and FFF8AB40 b2 are set (05F080 otherwise, not defined here). Counts passes in FFF8AB5A while cruise is active (FFF88E12 b1) without pedal override (88E12 b5), FFF88E28 b0 / 88A26 b0 clear, manifold pressure FFF88A34 >= cal 0x409FC (53 kPa) and acceleration FFF8B9C2 >= this(speed); more than cal 0x409FE (10 passes, 0.2 s) sets FFF8AB43 b3, which ends cruise via 0x16E314 (inferred: runaway-acceleration check). Stock 21.6 km/h/s up to 40 km/h, 16.2 at 60, 10.8 km/h/s at 80 km/h. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05F074 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00E1DC. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Cruise Acceleration Cancel Threshold (Meter Cruise Option)
table.description:
With one cruise option only: if the car accelerates faster than this (by speed) for 3 s while cruise is on, cruise is cancelled and stays unavailable for the rest of the drive (probably a runaway check). Stock 20 km/h/s at low speed down to 4 km/h/s at 200 km/h.
Details: When used: only with the meter flag FFF811E1 bit 4 ('Meter Cruise Option', CAN 0x282) and FFF88BB2 bit 2, while cruise is active (FFF88E12 bit 1) and has been for cal 0x35C02 = 200 passes without FFF88E12 bit 5. 0x119200 (read; 10 ms task via 0x110AAC; arguments from the call at seg_0x110000:601): FFF8A8A4 bit 3 is set after cal 0x35C00 = 300 passes (3 s) of FFF8B3F8 > cal 0x35BFC (24000 = 74 ft-lb, 100 Nm) together with either (a) the acceleration FFF88E78 > this(cruise vehicle speed FFF8B9F4), or (b) speed above the set speed FFF8B9FA by more than cal 0x35BFE (3 km/h) for 200 passes, no raise/lower switch edge (FFF88E11 bits 4/5) for 200 passes and FFF88E78 > cal 0x35BFA (1.75 km/h/s). FFF8A8A4 bit 3 latches FFF88E13 bit 4 for the rest of the drive (0x11BCA8, never cleared, read), which with the meter flag and the main switch sets FFF8AB43 bit 6 (0x16DED0) and that clears the cruise-engaged bit FFF88E12 bit 0 (0x16F194) (read): cruise is cancelled and stays unavailable. FFF8B3F8 = CAN 0x161 bytes 1:0 (FFF88BAE) x 8 - 64000 in torque_nm units (0x10E640, read; which unit sends it is not identified). FFF88E78 = speed change over 1.01 s in km/h x 128 (0x06B526, read). Stock 20.3 km/h/s up to 40 km/h, 8.0 at 80, 7.0 at 120, 6.3 at 160, 4.0 km/h/s at 200 km/h. Physical purpose (runaway / unexpected acceleration check) inferred. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05D6D8 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00C580. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Cruise Speed Error Gain (State 0xC0)
table.description:
Cruise controller gain used in a cruise state probably linked to the lowering switch (inferred), when Cruise Speed Error Gain (Set-Speed Approach) is not active. Stock flat 160.
Details: Cruise module 0x165AC4/0x1663AC, 20 ms task (read). 0x16AF7C (read): the cruise speed controller multiplies the speed error (target FFF8B9DC - speed FFF8B9F4) by a gain from one of seven tables, selected by the cruise state FFF8AB58 (state machine 0x168AC2) and flags: AB3D b0/b1 -> 05EE58; else state 0x23 -> 05EE1C; state 0xB0 -> 05EE44; state 0xC0, or any other state while the speed is not within 2 km/h of the maximum cruise speed FFF8B9F0 (86B5F): AB42 b2 -> 05EE94, else state 0x40 -> 05EE80, state 0xC0 -> this; otherwise (incl. the hold state 0x33) -> 05EE30. Axes: vehicle acceleration FFF8B9C2 and speed error. The gain x 05EED0-family(rpm)/160 is filtered into FFF8C5BE, which is integrated with the error into the drive-torque command FFF8C438 -> FFF8B9E2. State 0xC0 is entered on FFF8AB3F bit 6 (0x170164) (read); the lower-switch side by the state numbering (inferred, group_C). Used only while FFF8AB42 bit 2 is clear (otherwise Set-Speed Approach). Stock flat 160 (no error or acceleration dependence). LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05EE6C by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00DFC0. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Brake Override Pedal Limit Ramp-Down Rate
table.description:
How fast, by vehicle speed, brake override ramps the accelerator signal down. Larger = faster torque cut when brake and accelerator overlap. Stock 14-18 % pedal per second. Part of the brake override, which limits the accelerator signal when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held.
Details: When used: while brake override is active (FFF8AC8F bit 0). Brake override module 0x181B38 (10 ms task 0x1DFE3C, read): it limits the accelerator pedal that feeds the torque request, FFF88A5E = min(pedal FFF88EE6, limit FFF8BAFA) (0x09E800, read), when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held. Brake detection: VDC CAN frame 0x0D1 byte 2 (FFF88DF9, slew-limited 8/pass into FFF8AC94; brake pressure, inferred) against a threshold, or discrete input FFF88E2F bit 3 (pin PF10; brake switch, inferred) when the pressure signal is not valid (FFF8AC8F bit 4 clear). Vehicle speed FFF8AC95 = km/h from the wheel speeds or FFF88BE8 x 9/160 (0x182E34, read). The module sets no DTC (no DTC monitor record points at its RAM, read). 0x182900 (read, lookup by speed FFF8AC95 checked in the assembly at 0x182A6E): limit FFF8BAFA = max(previous limit - this, Brake Override Pedal Limit Floor), capped at cal 0x433B6 = 26214 (40 % pedal); if the pedal is below the limit the limit follows the pedal. FFF88A5E = min(pedal, limit). Stock 92, 92, 105, 118 per pass at 30/60/90/120 km/h = 14, 14, 16, 18 % pedal per second. Larger = faster torque cut when brake and accelerator overlap. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05F24C by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00E3D4. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Brake Override Pedal Limit Floor
table.description:
Lowest pedal value, by vehicle speed, that brake override ramps the accelerator signal down to. Stock 1-3 % pedal. Part of the brake override, which limits the accelerator signal when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held.
Details: When used: while brake override is active (FFF8AC8F bit 0). Brake override module 0x181B38 (10 ms task 0x1DFE3C, read): it limits the accelerator pedal that feeds the torque request, FFF88A5E = min(pedal FFF88EE6, limit FFF8BAFA) (0x09E800, read), when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held. Brake detection: VDC CAN frame 0x0D1 byte 2 (FFF88DF9, slew-limited 8/pass into FFF8AC94; brake pressure, inferred) against a threshold, or discrete input FFF88E2F bit 3 (pin PF10; brake switch, inferred) when the pressure signal is not valid (FFF8AC8F bit 4 clear). Vehicle speed FFF8AC95 = km/h from the wheel speeds or FFF88BE8 x 9/160 (0x182E34, read). The module sets no DTC (no DTC monitor record points at its RAM, read). 0x182900 (read, lookup by speed FFF8AC95, assembly 0x182A92): the lowest value the ramped pedal limit FFF8BAFA can reach (limit = max(previous - Ramp-Down Rate, this), then capped at 40 %). Stock 1966, 1311, 655, 655 = 3.0, 2.0, 1.0, 1.0 % pedal at 4/7/10/20 km/h. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05F258 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00E3E0. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Brake Override Recovery Rate (Pedal Held)
table.description:
How fast, by vehicle speed, the pedal limit is raised again after the brake is released while the driver keeps the accelerator pressed. Stock 50-100 % pedal per second. Part of the brake override, which limits the accelerator signal when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held.
Details: When used: after the brake is released (recovery FFF8AC90 bit 7) in recovery state FFF8AC8E = 1. Brake override module 0x181B38 (10 ms task 0x1DFE3C, read): it limits the accelerator pedal that feeds the torque request, FFF88A5E = min(pedal FFF88EE6, limit FFF8BAFA) (0x09E800, read), when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held. Brake detection: VDC CAN frame 0x0D1 byte 2 (FFF88DF9, slew-limited 8/pass into FFF8AC94; brake pressure, inferred) against a threshold, or discrete input FFF88E2F bit 3 (pin PF10; brake switch, inferred) when the pressure signal is not valid (FFF8AC8F bit 4 clear). Vehicle speed FFF8AC95 = km/h from the wheel speeds or FFF88BE8 x 9/160 (0x182E34, read). The module sets no DTC (no DTC monitor record points at its RAM, read). Recovery state machine 0x181748 (read): 4 at recovery start; 4 -> 3 when the pedal stayed within 9 % (cal 0x433A6) of its minimum since recovery began (FFF8BAD6) for 10 passes; 3 -> 1 when the limit FFF8BAFA >= 10 % (cal 0x433AA) and the override began while moving (FFF8AC8F bit 5, speed > 2 km/h); 1 -> 0 when the pedal rises 9 % above that minimum. 0x182900 (read, lookup by speed, assembly 0x182A00): in state 1 the limit rises by this each pass, capped by 05F27C (65535 stock). Stock 328, 328, 655, 655 at 0/40/80/120 km/h = 50, 50, 100, 100 % pedal per second. States 2-4 use 05F264 (655) and state 0 a time-based ramp (Brake Override Recovery Time). LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05F270 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00E3F8. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Brake Override Recovery Time
table.description:
Time, by vehicle speed, over which full pedal is restored after brake override ends (recovery ends early if the pedal is released or reached). Stock 0.3-0.5 s. Part of the brake override, which limits the accelerator signal when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held.
Details: When used: at the start of recovery (rising FFF8AC90 bit 7), latched into FFF8BB04 by 0x182DC0 (read; cal 0x43430 = 400 instead while the speed signal is faulty, FFF88E28 bit 0). Brake override module 0x181B38 (10 ms task 0x1DFE3C, read): it limits the accelerator pedal that feeds the torque request, FFF88A5E = min(pedal FFF88EE6, limit FFF8BAFA) (0x09E800, read), when the brake is applied while the accelerator is held. table.name: Engine Torque from Load (CAN, DAM 1.0)
table.description:

Only affects the maximum-available torque value the ECU sends over CAN to other modules (inferred meaning); it does not change fuel, spark, throttle or boost. table.name: CAN Engine Torque Fuel-Cut Fade Rate
table.description:
How fast, by rpm, the engine torque reported over CAN to other modules (for example stability control) fades out at a fuel cut and returns after it. It does not change fuelling or throttle. Stock slow at low rpm, instant at 8000 rpm.

A weight w = FFF854FC moves toward 0 while the cylinder fuel cut FFF8A64C bit 0 is set and toward 0xFF00 otherwise, by (target - w) x this/255 per pass (read). The DAM-blended engine torque FFF8B48A (= DAM x B490/16 + (16 - DAM) x B4A2/16, DAM FFF811AE) is scaled by w/0xFF00 about the 16000 zero point (B48E, read), and FFF8B404 = (that - 16000 - (05D3E4(rpm, FFF88AE6) + FFF8B46E + FFF8AF62 - 48000))/8 + 10000, i.e. faded torque minus loss terms in 10000 + 10 x Nm (read). FFF8B404 is packed into the engine CAN TX frames (0x08B1B6 / 0x08C220, bytes FFF8CC91/92) and is the 'actual torque' of the VDC torque-request loop 0x117778 (VDC Torque Request Correction); B48E and A8F0 (= w >> 8) have no readers (ram_xref, read). So this only shapes how fast the torque reported to the other control units falls at a fuel cut and returns after it; it does not change fuelling or the throttle directly. Stock 0.16 per pass at <= 800 rpm, 0.40 at 2000, 0.80 at 4000, 1.0 (instant) at 8000 rpm. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05D3D8 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00C280. table.name: MAF Sensor Scaling
table.description:
Converts MAF sensor voltage to airflow (g/s) in 64 fixed steps from 0 to 4.92 V; this airflow drives the ECU's air model, load and fuel. Rescale every point when fitting a bigger intake or a different MAF, and keep peak flow below the P0103 voltage limit (stock 4.79 V). An internal 218 g/s cap on one copy of the airflow affects only purge, TGV, monitors and similar side functions, not fuel, load or timing.
Details: When used: always (4 ms task prefix 0x1E2CB4, read). ADC channel 2 (0xFFFFE844) -> FFF8C990 (10-bit) x ADC trim FFF82038 / 32768, capped at 1023, x 64 -> FFF8CA48 -> FFF88A1A (0x1D87C8, read). FFF82038 is a per-unit gain trim copied at start from a stored data block (FFF81050, 0x1CF324) and used only within 125/128...131/128, else 1.0 (cals 0x28BA2 / 0x28BA3 / 0x28BA0, read); 65536 = 5 V (inferred). 0x06CA98 subtracts a start-up correction (only while FFF88CE5 is set) and floors at MAF Sensor Voltage Floor -> FFF88CFA; 0x06C9F8 looks up FFF88CFA >> 2 in this 64-point u32 table (boot routine 0x68EC: index = input / 256 with linear interpolation, input capped at 0x3F00, so above 4.92 V the last point holds) -> FFF8921C -> FFF88820 (the cal 0x57585 bit 7 filter is off in stock). g/s = value / 76800 (OBD PID 0x10 chain, read). The axis is implicit: point n is at n x 0.078125 V (0...4.92 V). FFF88820 feeds the manifold/airflow model 0x11D704 / 0x11D4E4, which the load and fuel calculations use, and the torque model 0x0C3E34 (read). Stock 1.4 g/s up to 0.47 V, 312.6 g/s at 4.77 V, 355.3 g/s at 4.92 V. For a bigger housing or another MAF, rescale every point to the new g/s at that voltage and keep peak flow below MAF Sensor Voltage High Limit (stock 4.79 V = 318 g/s on the stock curve; P0103 after 13 passes). Limits elsewhere (read): the scan-tool/OBD MAF value FFF88A4A saturates at 300 g/s, and FFF8B4D6, a u16 copy of the model's air quantity (g/s x 300), saturates at 218 g/s (0x11DEE0). That 218 g/s cap does not limit fuel, load, ignition or boost. The base fuel quantity (0x0B8030) and engine load (0x0B7EFC) are computed from the unsaturated cylinder flow FFF8C250, and no ignition routine reads FFF8B4D6. Its readers are: the evap purge module (0x0D4C14, 0x0D4E78: purge flow = purge rate x air) and the evap monitor 0x18C3B0; TGV request logic and TGV transition fuel (0x10D93C, 0x0CA144); the EGR fresh-air option (0x0FA7C4, off in stock); the torque model's air-path lag lookup (0x0C34F8, axis ends at 208 g/s); the exhaust temperature model's filter and fuel-cut terms (0x0C9878, axis ends at 210 g/s); catalyst/rear-O2 heater energy and OBD monitor enables (0x101CF0, 0x134374, 0x1B3280, 0x1B3A48, 0x1259EC, 0x09FE44); charging control (0x136CD8, 0x13741C); the 'air since start' sum 0x10A270; and the CAN full-load air estimate 0x110444. All of these use thresholds far below 218 g/s, or axes whose last breakpoint is below it. The only one that can still change above 218 g/s is the CAN estimate, which takes the larger of FFF8B4D6 and its own value (inferred: little effect). The limits that matter at high airflow are the 4.92 V end of this table, MAF Sensor Voltage High Limit, the 256 % (3.31 g/rev) ceiling of engine load (0x0B7EFC) and Base Fuel Quantity Limit; the model's cylinder flow FFF8C250 itself does not saturate. Identical in both images. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 028BDC by the code that reads it (read). Data at 03111C. Confidence: read.

table.name: MAP Sensor Multiplier
table.description:
Gain of the manifold pressure sensor conversion, in kPa per volt (stock 63 kPa per volt). For a 3-bar or larger sensor set it to the new sensor's slope and set MAP Sensor Offset to match. The ECU's MAP value cannot go above 256 kPa absolute (about 22 psi boost at sea level) whatever sensor is fitted, so anything higher reads as 256 kPa.
Details: When used: always (2 ms task prefix 0x1E2AA2; also 0x1E220A / 0x1E4D00 at start-up, read). MAP (kPa x 256) = ADC channel 18 sample FFF88D3A (16-bit left-justified 10-bit value, not corrected by the ADC trim FFF82038) x this >> 8 + MAP Sensor Offset, limited to 0...65535 (0x6E00, read) -> FFF8913C, the MAP the engine uses (-> FFF88A34 -> FFF88666; FFF8869C for the airflow model) and FFF89040 / FFF89A32 (OBD MAP). FFF89140 = the same minus 0xD4C (13.3 kPa), limited the same way, is the boost-control pressure FFF88FF4. With 65536 = 5 V (inferred) the unit is kPa per volt = value / 5: stock 315 = 63 kPa/V, so with the stock offset 0.5 V = 7.9 kPa and 4.5 V = 259.9 kPa. Hard limit (read): the MAP value cannot exceed 255.99 kPa absolute (about 22.3 psi gauge at sea level) whatever sensor is fitted; with stock scaling that is reached at 4.44 V, and the boost-control copy saturates at 269.3 kPa actual MAP. To fit a different (e.g. 3-bar) sensor: this = sensor slope in kPa per V x 5, and MAP Sensor Offset = sensor kPa at 0 V x 256; example 0.5 V = 20 kPa, 4.5 V = 300 kPa -> 70 kPa/V -> 350, offset -15 kPa -> -3840. Readings above 256 kPa are still clipped. Range faults use raw voltage: P0107 below MAP Sensor Voltage Low Limit, P0108 above MAP Sensor Voltage High Limit; while the MAP fault flag FFF88E28 bit 3 is set MAP = cal 0x58EA4 x FFF8ADF0 / 32768 instead (read). The TMAP's temperature element is probably Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 (change that table too if the new sensor's thermistor differs). LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 058EA0 by the code that reads it (read). Address 062B70. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: MAP Sensor Offset
table.description:
Offset of the manifold pressure sensor conversion (stock -23.6 kPa), i.e. the sensor's reading extrapolated to 0 V. Set it together with MAP Sensor Multiplier when fitting a different MAP sensor. The result is still limited to 256 kPa absolute.
Details: When used: always (2 ms task prefix 0x1E2AA2, read): offset of the MAP conversion in kPa x 256, added to sample x MAP Sensor Multiplier >> 8 before the result is limited to 0...65535 (255.99 kPa). Equals the sensor's (extrapolated) reading at 0 V. Stock -6048 = -23.6 kPa. For a different sensor: offset = kPa at 0 V x 256 = (kPa at V1 - slope x V1) x 256; example 0.5 V = 20 kPa, 4.5 V = 300 kPa -> -15 kPa -> -3840. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 058EA2 by the code that reads it (read). Address 062B72. Confidence: read.

table.name: MAF Sensor Voltage Floor
table.description:
Lowest value the corrected MAF voltage may reach after the ECU subtracts its post-start MAF correction (a decaying start-up offset); it applies at all times after the first pass. Stock 0.4 V. Normally leave alone.
Details: Lower limit of the dynamically corrected MAF voltage FFF88CFA (0x06CA98, read). The correction (voltage minus a gain x rate term, cal 0x5758E/0x57590/0x57587) only runs while FFF88CE5 is set. Stock 0.4 V. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 057592 by the code that reads it (read). Address 0611DA. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Intake Air Temp Sensor Scaling
table.description:
Converts the main intake air temperature sensor voltage to degrees; this IAT feeds the timing, boost and fuel compensations and the scan-tool reading. Its voltage axis is shared with Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 Scaling, so edit only the temperatures when fitting a different sensor.
Details: When used: always (10 ms task prefix 0x1E2F20 / 0x06AF58, read). ADC channel 19 (0xFFFFE864, untrimmed) -> FFF88D38 -> FFF88F30, filtered by cal 0x579B6 (65535 = no filter in stock) -> FFF88F34 / FFF88F32, looked up here (boot lookup 0x7250) to give FFF88662 = degC + 50: the OBD IAT FFF8CEE5, the IAT behind FFF88A48 (the IAT axis of the timing, boost, throttle and fuel compensation tables) and the IAT read by fuel 0x0C589C and purge 0x0D4E78 (for Purge Air Density (IAT, Baro), 0x0D44DC) (read). This is IAT sensor 1 (P0112 / P0113, read), probably the element in the MAF housing (inferred). The voltage axis (0x579FC, 32 points 0...4.96 V in 0.16 V steps; 65536 = 5 V inferred) is shared with Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 Scaling: change only the temperature values for a different thermistor, or both sensors move. While the sensor is faulted (FFF88E28 bit 2) the fixed voltage cal 0x579BA x 256 (stock 3.40 V, about 20 C) is used. Stock: 205 C at 0 V, 25 C at 3.20 V, -50 C from 4.80 V (identical to IAT 2). LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 060850 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor boot 0633A4. Confidence: read.

table.name: Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 Scaling
table.description:
Converts the second intake temperature sensor's voltage to degrees. This is the air temperature the ECU's airflow model uses to work out air density, and it probably comes from the manifold pressure (TMAP) sensor, so update it when you swap that sensor for one with a different thermistor. Its voltage axis is shared with the main IAT table; change only the temperatures.
Details: When used: always (10 ms task prefix 0x1E2F20 / 0x06B304, read). ADC channel 20 (0xFFFFE868, untrimmed) -> FFF88D40 -> FFF88F36, filtered by cal 0x579B8 (no filter in stock) -> FFF88F38 / FFF88F3A, looked up here (boot lookup 0x7250) into FFF888CF (degC + 50; FFF888D4 from the unfaulted value). This is IAT sensor 2 (P0097 / P0098 monitors on the same voltage, read). FFF888CF is the air temperature of the speed-density airflow model (0x11DF4C: density from MAP and IAT 2 + 223 K) and is also read by requested torque 0x0BE694, ignition 0x0D98F8 / 0x0D9A10 / 0x0DE0E0 and AVCS 0x15969C (read), so a wrong curve shifts the modelled air and load. Probably the thermistor of the manifold TMAP sensor (inferred from its use as the manifold air temperature): when fitting a different TMAP / MAP sensor with its own thermistor, change these temperature values. The voltage axis (0x579FC) is shared with Intake Air Temp Sensor Scaling, so change only the data. While faulted (FFF88FCD bit 2) the fixed voltage cal 0x579BB x 256 (stock 3.40 V, about 20 C) is used. Stock identical to IAT 1. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 06085C by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor boot 0633B0. Confidence: read.

table.name: Coolant Temp Sensor Scaling
table.description:
Converts coolant temperature sensor voltage to degrees. Every coolant-based table and the scan-tool coolant reading use this. Change only when fitting a different sensor.
Details: When used: always (40 ms task prefix 0x1E43FE / 0x06BA46, read). Coolant sensor voltage FFF8865E (input 0 of the 8-way multiplexer on ADC channel 21, untrimmed, 65536 = 5 V inferred) is filtered by cal 0x56EE8 (65535 = no filter) into FFF88ADC and looked up here (boot lookup 0x73BC) into FFF88AE8 / FFF88AE0 (256 x (degC + 50)): FFF8CD65 (coolant byte, degC + 50), the OBD coolant value and FFF88A44 (the coolant axis of most tables). While the sensor is faulted (FFF88E28 bit 1) a warm-up model from cals 0x56EEC-0x56EF2 replaces it. Range faults: P0117 below Coolant Temp Sensor Voltage Low Limit, P0118 above Coolant Temp Sensor Voltage High Limit. Stock: 205 C at 0 V, 25.7 C at 3.20 V, -50 C from 4.80 V. Change only when fitting a different sensor. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 060874 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor boot 0633C8. Confidence: read.

table.name: Oil Temp Sensor Scaling
table.description:
Converts oil temperature sensor voltage to degrees; this oil temperature feeds the AVCS and idle tables and the scan-tool reading. Change only when fitting a different sensor.
Details: When used: always (40 ms task prefix 0x1E43FE / 0x06BEA0, read). Oil temperature sensor voltage FFF88AA2 (input 7 of the 8-way multiplexer on ADC channel 21, untrimmed) is filtered by cal 0x56F76 (65535 = no filter) into FFF88AE4 and looked up here (boot lookup 0x73BC). Output unit 256 x (degC + 50), read: FFF88E24 = (output - 0xA00) x 256 / 205 and OBD PID 0x5C reports FFF88E24 x 205 / 65536 = degC + 40. FFF88E24 / FFF88E26 is the oil temperature of the AVCS and idle tables (oil_temp_obd axis). Range faults: P0197 below Oil Temp Sensor Voltage Low Limit, P0198 above Oil Temp Sensor Voltage High Limit. Stock identical to the coolant curve. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 060880 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor boot 0633D4. Confidence: read.

table.name: A/F Sensor Scaling (Wide Range)
table.description:
Converts the front wideband A/F sensor signal to lambda when the reading is outside about lambda 0.90-1.37. This is the measured lambda used by closed loop fueling. Identical to A/F Sensor Scaling (Near Stoich) in stock; edit both together.
Details: When used: Used while FFF88AFB bit 4 is clear: the A/F signal is outside about lambda 0.90-1.37 (window -800..1000 with hysteresis 333, 0x0843F8, read); gain cal 0x571F0 = 2. Identical to Near Stoich in stock; edit both together. 0x06C1A8 (read): the A/F sensor signal FFF88B2E is looked up here (boot lookup 0x6A0C) into FFF88AF6, the measured lambda of the closed loop (B308 = 43194 x 32768 / FFF88AF6, 0x0FF3CC). Stock lambda 1.00 at signal -25...0. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 06088C by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor boot 0633E0. Confidence: read.

table.name: A/F Sensor Scaling (Near Stoich)
table.description:
Converts the front A/F sensor signal to lambda when it reads within about lambda 0.90-1.37, at a higher gain. Shares its axis with A/F Sensor Scaling (Wide Range) and is identical to it in stock; edit both together.
Details: When used: Used while the A/F signal is within about lambda 0.90-1.37 (FFF88AFB bit 4 set, 0x0843F8, read); higher gain cal 0x571F1 = 9 (gain reading inferred). Second A/F sensor table in 0x06C1A8 (read); shares the axis with A/F Sensor Scaling (Wide Range). Identical to it in stock; edit both together. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 060898 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor boot 0633EC. Confidence: read.

table.name: Fuel Level Sensor Scaling
table.description:
Converts the fuel sender reading, which the instrument cluster sends to the ECU over CAN, to fuel level (219 = 100 %). The ECU averages it and reports it as fuel level to a scan tool. Stock: full at the lowest input, empty at the highest.
Details: When used: always (0x06C336, read). Input: the fuel sender reading sent by the combination meter on CAN 0x282 bytes 0-1 (10-bit, FFF88E04 -> 0x1108B8 -> FFF8B43C; not an ECU analog input). 0x06C336 forms FFF88BD0 = FFF8B43C x 2867 / (FFF8B43C + cal 0x572E0 (720)), filters it into FFF88BCC and looks it up here (boot lookup 0x7250) into FFF88BD4; FFF88BD7 is its average over cal 0x572E6 samples taken while FFF88A76 is at least cal 0x572E4, kept in backup RAM FFF806BB/806BC, and reported by OBD PID 0x2F as x 255 / 219 (read). So this is the fuel level curve, 219 = 100 %. P0463 / P0462 when FFF88BCC is above cal 0x572DA / below cal 0x572DE (0x0714E0 / 0x071548, read). Stock: full (219) at the lowest input, empty at 2432 and above. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 0608A4 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor boot 0633F8. Confidence: read.

table.name: Battery Temperature Sensor Scaling
table.description:
Converts the battery temperature sensor voltage to degrees for the charging-voltage control. It is probably the temperature half of the battery sensor, whose current signal the ECU also reads. Leave alone unless the battery sensor is changed.
Details: When used: always (10 ms task prefix 0x1E2F20 / 0x06C768, read). ADC channel 9 (0xFFFFE852, untrimmed) -> FFF8939A, filtered by cal 0x590F0 into FFF8939E (cal 0x590EE replaces the input while FFF88BCA bit 2 or 3 is set) and looked up here (boot lookup 0x7250) into FFF893A0 (degC + 50), read only by the charging-voltage control 0x136CD8 (temperature-compensated voltage targets); the unfiltered value gives FFF893A1, reported by SSM as x - 10 (0x11F0E8, read). Identity (inferred): its companion input ADC channel 4 (FFF89390, 0x06C554) is a linear signal centred on 2.5 V (FFF89396 = 12800 - 0.488 x (sample - 32768); SSM x/128 + 28 puts zero at 2.5 V, about -50 A per volt), i.e. a bidirectional battery current, read by charging control 0x136BC0 and idle 0x0EE338; the two inputs share their filter cal block and their range monitors (FFF88BCA bits 2-5, 0x0715B0-0x07175C) are both enabled by cal 0x57584 bit 4, which is clear in stock (monitors off). A current + temperature pair used only for charging is the battery sensor, so this is battery temperature. Stock: 100 C at 0.32 V, 20 C at 2.37 V, -40 C from 4.71 V (NTC). Leave alone unless the battery sensor is changed. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 0608B0 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor boot 063404. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: Rear O2 Sensor Ready Heater Energy Threshold
table.scaling: rear O2 heater drive (accumulated counts) uint16
table.description:
How much heater energy, by coolant temperature at start, the rear O2 sensor must have received before it is treated as warmed up and ready. Raising it delays the rear O2 sensor (and its diagnostics) becoming active. Stock about 130 s of heating at -40 C to about 90 s at 60 C.
Details: When used: while the engine runs (run state FFF8906B = 3). 0x1028D0 (read; called from 0x101CF0): FFF8A833 bit 7 is set (and held until the run state leaves 3) when the accumulated rear O2 heater drive FFF88E6E > this(coolant at start FFF88A46; the -40 C row is used when the coolant sensor is faulted, FFF88E28 bit 1), or when FFF8881E >= cal 0x4B900 (9437) for cal 0x4B904 (50) passes. Rear O2 identity: the heater output FFF9980E bit 2 is driven by 0x06EC70 for FFF8CE0B of every 24 40-ms passes, and 0x073570 monitors that output against FFF8CE0B into FFF89CB4 bits 0/1, the P0037 / P0038 (heater circuit, bank 1 sensor 2) monitor records (dtc_monitors slots 182 / 180, read). FFF88E6E sums FFF8CE0B every 40 ms (0x06ED92, read), so it is heater energy since start; FFF8CE0B = 0 while the heater is held off (initial delay from 0x608F4, high load, battery out of range; 0x06E7D8, read). FFF8881E = 2 x (ADC channel 11 - ADC channel 25) (0x1E0000 task, read); it is the oxygen-sensor signal that gates Fuel Cut Recovery Enrichment (0x0CAE40: FFF8881E < cal 0x14F5C, read), so the second path is 'sensor already reads rich' (inferred). FFF8A833 bit 7 feeds the catalyst/rear-O2 module 0x101CF0 (0x1023E0, 0x102B58) and the rear O2 diagnostics 0x1B8890 / 0x1B902C (P0137, result FFF8AD93 bit 7) and 0x123C68 (read). Meaning 'sensor ready / warmed up' inferred. Stock 26250 at -40 C falling to 18125 at 60 C start coolant; at 13.75 V with the default heater stage that is about 130 s and 90 s of heating (inferred, 200 counts/s). Raising it delays the rear O2 sensor being treated as ready. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05CEB0 by the code that reads it (read). Descriptor 00BC9C. Confidence: inferred.

table.name: MAP Sensor Voltage Low Limit (P0107)
table.description:
Sensor voltage below which the MAP sensor is flagged as shorted low (P0107) and a substitute MAP is used. It works on raw voltage, so it does not change when you rescale the MAP sensor. Stock 0.36 V.
Details: When used: always while the monitor is enabled (FFF88E66 bit 1, FFF89183 = 0). 0x06FC80 (read): P0107 (FFF89B0B bit 2, record slot of P0107) is set when the MAP sensor sample FFF88D3A (ADC channel 18, 16-bit left-justified, not trimmed) stays below this for cal 0x56702 (200) passes; while set the ECU replaces MAP by cal 0x58EA4 x FFF8ADF0 / 32768 (fault flag FFF88E28 bit 3, read in 0x1E2AA2). It compares raw voltage, so it does not move when MAP Sensor Multiplier / Offset are changed. Stock 4697 = 0.358 V (with stock scaling -1.0 kPa). A replacement sensor whose lowest output (engine-off vacuum is not reached, so the lowest is about 20-30 kPa) is above this needs no change. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 056708 by the code that reads it (read). Address 060350. Confidence: read.

table.name: MAP Sensor Voltage High Limit (P0108)
table.description:
Sensor voltage above which the MAP sensor is flagged as shorted high (P0108). Raw voltage, independent of the MAP scaling. Stock 4.84 V.
Details: When used: always while the monitor is enabled (FFF88E66 bit 1, FFF89183 = 0). 0x06FC80 (read): P0108 (FFF89B0B bit 1) is set when the MAP sensor sample FFF88D3A stays above this for cal 0x56703 (200) passes; the substitute MAP is then used (FFF88E28 bit 3). Raw voltage, independent of MAP Sensor Multiplier / Offset. Stock 63499 = 4.845 V. Note the MAP value itself is limited to 255.99 kPa (see MAP Sensor Multiplier) whatever the voltage. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05670A by the code that reads it (read). Address 060352. Confidence: read.

table.name: MAF Sensor Voltage Low Limit (P0102)
table.description:
MAF voltage below which the MAF circuit-low code P0102 is set. Stock 0.12 V; normally leave alone.
Details: When used: with the ignition/run input on (FFF8A297 bit 1) for at least cal 0x5700D (26) passes and FFF88E66 bit 1 set. 0x070048 (read): P0102 (FFF89AFC bit 6) is set when the MAF voltage FFF88D48 (ADC channel 2 sample x 64, before the ADC trim and before the start-up correction) has been below this for cal 0x57007 (13) passes, cleared after cal 0x57008 (13) passes above. Stock 1587 = 0.121 V. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05700E by the code that reads it (read). Address 060C56. Confidence: read.

table.name: MAF Sensor Voltage High Limit (P0103)
table.description:
MAF voltage above which the MAF circuit-high code P0103 is set. Stock 4.79 V, about 318 g/s on the stock MAF curve; with a larger intake keep peak flow below this voltage.
Details: When used: with the ignition/run input on (FFF8A297 bit 1) for at least cal 0x57009 (26) passes and FFF88E66 bit 1 set. 0x06FF70 (read): P0103 (FFF89AFC bit 5) is set when the MAF voltage FFF88D48 (ADC channel 2 x 64, untrimmed) has been above this for cal 0x57007 (13) passes, cleared after cal 0x57008 (13) passes below. Stock 62760 = 4.788 V, which on the stock MAF Sensor Scaling is 318 g/s. With a larger MAF housing make sure peak flow stays below this voltage (the scaling table itself stops at 4.92 V); raising it towards 4.9 V is possible but leaves less margin to detect a shorted signal (inferred). LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05700A by the code that reads it (read). Address 060C52. Confidence: read.

table.name: Intake Air Temp Sensor Voltage Low Limit (P0112)
table.description:
Voltage below which the main IAT sensor is flagged as shorted (reads impossibly hot, P0112). Stock 0.22 V; normally leave alone.
Details: When used: while FFF88E66 bit 1 is set and FFF89185 = 0. 0x070310 (read): P0112 (IAT circuit low, FFF89AFD bit 6) is set when the IAT sensor voltage FFF88D38 (ADC channel 19 x 64, untrimmed) is below this for cal 0x566F0 (13) passes. Low voltage = very hot reading (NTC). Stock 2927 = 0.223 V (about 170 C on the stock curve). While the IAT is faulted (FFF88E28 bit 2) the ECU looks up the fixed voltage cal 0x579BA x 256 (stock 174 = 3.40 V, about 20 C) instead (0x06AF58, read). LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05701A by the code that reads it (read). Address 060C62. Confidence: read.

table.name: Intake Air Temp Sensor Voltage High Limit (P0113)
table.description:
Voltage above which the main IAT sensor is flagged as open (reads impossibly cold, P0113). Stock 4.72 V; normally leave alone.
Details: When used: while FFF88E66 bit 1 is set and FFF89185 = 0. 0x0702A8 (read): P0113 (IAT circuit high, FFF89AFD bit 5) is set when the IAT sensor voltage FFF88D38 (ADC channel 19) is above this for cal 0x566F1 (13) passes. High voltage = open circuit / very cold. Stock 61815 = 4.716 V (about -43 C on the stock curve). LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 057018 by the code that reads it (read). Address 060C60. Confidence: read.

table.name: Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 Voltage Low Limit (P0097)
table.description:
Voltage below which the second intake temperature sensor is flagged as shorted (P0097). Stock 0.22 V; check it if a replacement TMAP sensor has a different thermistor.
Details: When used: while FFF88E66 bit 1 is set and FFF89188 = 0. 0x0703D4 (read): P0097 (IAT sensor 2 circuit low, FFF89B17 bit 0) is set when the IAT 2 sensor voltage FFF88D40 (ADC channel 20 x 64, untrimmed) is below this for cal 0x57014 (13) passes. While IAT 2 is faulted (FFF88FCD bit 2) the fixed voltage cal 0x579BB x 256 (stock 174 = 3.40 V, about 20 C) is used (0x06B304, read). Stock 2927 = 0.223 V. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 057016 by the code that reads it (read). Address 060C5E. Confidence: read.

table.name: Intake Air Temp Sensor 2 Voltage High Limit (P0098)
table.description:
Voltage above which the second intake temperature sensor is flagged as open (P0098). Stock 4.72 V; check it if a replacement TMAP sensor has a different thermistor.
Details: When used: while FFF88E66 bit 1 is set and FFF89188 = 0. 0x070378 (read): P0098 (IAT sensor 2 circuit high, FFF89B17 bit 1) is set when the IAT 2 sensor voltage FFF88D40 (ADC channel 20) is above this for cal 0x57010 (13) passes. Stock 61815 = 4.716 V. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 057012 by the code that reads it (read). Address 060C5A. Confidence: read.

table.name: Coolant Temp Sensor Voltage Low Limit (P0117)
table.description:
Voltage below which the coolant sensor is flagged as shorted (P0117). Stock 0.33 V; normally leave alone.
Details: When used: while FFF88E66 bit 1 is set and FFF8918B = 0. 0x070520 (read): P0117 (FFF89AFC bit 1) is set when the coolant sensor voltage FFF8865E (multiplexed ADC channel 21, input 0, untrimmed) is below this for cal 0x566F2 (13) passes. Stock 4291 = 0.327 V (about 141 C on the stock curve). While the coolant sensor is faulted (FFF88E28 bit 1) the coolant value follows a warm-up model instead (cals 0x56EEC-0x56EF2, 0x06BA46, read). LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05701E by the code that reads it (read). Address 060C66. Confidence: read.

table.name: Coolant Temp Sensor Voltage High Limit (P0118)
table.description:
Voltage above which the coolant sensor is flagged as open (P0118). Stock 4.71 V; normally leave alone.
Details: When used: while FFF88E66 bit 1 is set and FFF8918B = 0. 0x0704B8 (read): P0118 (FFF89AFC bit 0) is set when the coolant sensor voltage FFF8865E is above this for cal 0x566F3 (13) passes. Stock 61769 = 4.713 V (about -42 C). LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05701C by the code that reads it (read). Address 060C64. Confidence: read.

table.name: Oil Temp Sensor Voltage Low Limit (P0197)
table.description:
Voltage below which the oil temperature sensor is flagged as shorted (P0197). Stock 0.18 V; normally leave alone.

Stock 2411 = 0.184 V. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 05703C by the code that reads it (read). Address 060C84. Confidence: read.

table.name: Oil Temp Sensor Voltage High Limit (P0198)

Voltage above which the oil temperature sensor is flagged as open (P0198). Stock 4.71 V; normally leave alone.
Details: When used: while FFF88E66 bit 1 is set and FFF8919F = 0. 0x070588 (read): P0198 (FFF89B1D bit 7) is set when the oil temperature sensor voltage FFF88AA2 is above this for cal 0x57037 (13) passes. Stock 61769 = 4.713 V. LF9C100P: located from LF75404S 057038 by the code that reads it (read). Address 060C80. Confidence: read.

table.name: Rail Pressure Sensor Voltage Low Limit (P0192)
